News.title: Ex political advisor admits fraud over expense claims
News.content:
A former advisor to a Labour MP has admitted claiming fraudulent expenses on the Parliamentary travel booking system.

Matthew Torbitt worked for Bury South MP Christian Wakeford when, between August 2022 and September 2024, he claimed rail tickets that were "not for Parliamentary purposes", Thames Magistrates' Court heard.

He also admitted making a false claim for travel and accommodation expenses on 2 October 2024.

Torbitt, 35, has most recently worked as a political commentator and regularly appears on programmes including GB News, LBC, Sky News, BBC Newsnight, and Times Radio.

Prosecutor Maisha Mannan told the court the claims totalled more than Â£6,000, according to an early estimate by the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), but the exact sum will be calculated at a later date.

Torbitt, who appeared in court dressed in a navy blue suit, pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud by false representation.

District Judge Navneet Sher sent the case to Snaresbrook Crown Court for sentence at a later date, which has yet to be fixed.

"It's unlikely to be before four weeks, in any event," she told the defendant.

Torbitt worked in various advisory roles for Labour frontbenchers between 2018 and 2024.

An investigation was launched after police received a report that a member of staff working for an MP had allegedly made unauthorised purchases through a travel booking system, the Metropolitan Police previously said.

He was charged by postal requisition on 9 June.

Torbitt is engaged to women's rights activist and 2021 Love Island contestant Sharon Gaffka.

The couple welcomed a baby boy earlier this month, according to Torbitt's Instagram page.

News.title: Seattle mass shooting victims identified, including mom, 56, who was in line for cotton candy when gunfire broke out
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

The three people who died in Sunday’s mass shooting at a Seattle food festival have been identified by officials, including a 19-year-old police believe engaged in the gunfight.

There were at least three suspects involved and a 15-year-old was detained in connection with the shooting near Seattle’s iconic Space Needle Sunday evening. Police are still searching for at least one other unknown suspect.

Carlos Israel Sanchez Villalba, 44, and 56-year-old Ashley Whitehead died in the shooting, the King County Medical Examiner said, along with 19-year-old Junior Cee Niko Semo.

Four others were injured, including a toddler, and the three adults have since been discharged from the hospital. The two-year-old boy was said to be in a satisfactory condition as of Monday evening.

The 15-year-old is being held in juvenile detention for investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault.

open image in gallery Law enforcement believes the mass shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival occurred because two suspects were shooting at each other ( Getty )

Shots rang out at the annual Bite of Seattle event, a street food and live music event for families held at the Seattle Center, a 74-acre entertainment and cultural complex downtown.

The attack is the latest of at least 271 mass shootings that have been recorded in the U.S. this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive.

What happened?

The festival was winding down at around 6. p.m. when the suspects started firing at one another, Seattle Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said. Dozens of officers were providing security at the event and witnessed the shooting.

A large number of police and emergency crews responded and began evacuating the area around the sprawling Seattle Center campus as festival-goers took cover.

Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just bought crepes from a vendor when the shooting started nearby, prompting her group to seek shelter in the nearby Seattle Children’s Museum.

open image in gallery Shortly after the mass shooting, police led a potential suspect away ( Reuters )

open image in gallery The entrance to the site at the Seattle Center, cordoned off with police tape following Sunday’s outbreak of gun violence ( Getty )

“We were right next to him when it started, so we took off running,” she said. “So we took off running too into the building with the crowd.”

Amid the chaos, many vendors bolted toward the exits, abandoning their stalls. Hours afterward, some gathered around the police tape, wondering when they would be allowed to return to collect their tents, food and cooking equipment.

One of the vendors, Roberto Ramirez, said he heard what sounded like firecrackers before people began yelling “shooter” and running frantically.

“Suddenly everything was empty,” he said. “People were freaked out.”

open image in gallery Seattle Police have said that the two people responsible may have been shooting at each other, not aiming for visitors to the food festival ( AP )

After the initial panic, new visitors continued to arrive, unaware of what had happened, and were instructed to leave by police, he said.

Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and turned to see a rush of people fleeing.

“People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling,” Wakonabo said.

“Once I heard a ‘pop, pop, pop,’ that’s when I knew it was a shooter,” he added, reporting that he later saw multiple victims on the ground.

The victims

Two victims, 44-year-old Carlos Israel Sanchez Villalba and a 56-year-old Ashley Whitehead, were killed in the gunfire, The Seattle Times reported, citing the King County Medical Examiner.

Sanchez Villalba died at the scene. Whitehead succumbed to her injuries after being transported to a hospital. FOX 13 Seattle reported that Sanchez Villalba died from a gunshot wound to the torso and Whitehead was shot multiple times in the pelvis.

At least four others were taken to hospital for treatment. Their identities have yet to be revealed.

As of Monday morning, three adults had been discharged and the two-year-old boy was in satisfactory condition but still under observation, a spokesperson for Harborview Medical Center told the Associated Press. The three who were discharged included a 23-year-old man, a 27-year-old man and a 39-year-old woman.

open image in gallery Seattle Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis have said his officers are ‘still trying to figure out’ precisely what happened ( Reuters )

A fifth person was treated at the scene for a minor injury.

Harborview said it had gone into “partial lockdown” following guidance from the Seattle Police Department.

The suspects

Police believe there were at least three suspects, according to court documents. Authorities only identified the teenager taken into custody as a 15-year-old.

One of the suspects was killed in the shooting, according to court documents. He was identified as 19-year-old Junior Cee Niko Semo of Seattle by the King County Medical Examiner Monday, per KING 5 News. He reportedly died of multiple gunshot wounds.

“Based on the evidence at the scene, investigators believe” the 15-year-old “and one of the deceased engaged in a gunfight with at least one other unknown suspect,” the document obtained by the Associated Press said.

Davis said officers do not yet have a description of the third suspect who fled, saying: “We’re still trying to figure this out.”

There is believed to be no further threat to the public.

The aftermath

open image in gallery Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson denounced the ‘act of horrific violence’ after the shooting devastating the community Sunday ( Reuters )

Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson called the shooting an “act of horrific violence.”

“Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire,” she said at a press conference.

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson wrote on X: “My prayers are with the families of the victims, and the responders as they work to keep people safe.”

Washington Democratic Rep. Pramila Jayapal said in a statement that she was “absolutely horrified” by the violence, calling it “senseless” and likewise expressing her condolences to the families of the victims.

The gun control advocacy group March for Our Lives said: “Our hearts are with everyone who was there tonight, and with a city that didn’t ask for this. We will not accept this as normal.”

Ariana Baio and Rachel Dobkin contributed to this report

America’s biggest cities are seeing a drastic decline in the number of children living there due to falling birth rates, the cost of living and safety concerns, according to analysis.

The number of children under 18 living in major cities is down six percent in the past decade, compared with a one percent decline nationwide, according to the Wall Street Journal.

The drop is even steeper among families with young kids — the number of children under 5 in big cities has fallen 15 percent, compared with a seven percent decline nationwide.

It comes as the number of births in the U.S. decreased by one percent last year, with more than 3.6 million births recorded, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Birth rates in large urban counties fell 18 percent between 2010 and 2024, according to an analysis by Connor O’Brien, a fellow at the Institute for Progress. It was the largest drop of any county type.

open image in gallery America’s biggest cities are seeing a drastic decline in the number of kids living there due to falling birth rates and several factors driving parents away ( Getty Images )

Aside from declining birth rates, big cities are also seeing families move due to concerns about costs, safety and quality of life, according to the WSJ.

San Jose, California, saw the number of children under 5 drop 34 percent in the last decade, the most of any large city.

Even relatively affordable cities are experiencing a decline. Albuquerque, New Mexico, for example, is seeing a 15 percent drop in the number of children, with about half of that figure due to more families leaving than arriving. And in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, the number of kids has declined 11 percent.

In New York City, the number of children is down eight percent over the past decade, the publication reported.

It could take about 65 years for a typical household living in New York City to afford a down payment of $265,000 on a home, according to an analysis released last month by retail mortgage lender Rocket Mortgage.

open image in gallery The decline in children is due to falling birth rates and several factors driving parents away, including affordability ( AFP via Getty Images )

“Local home prices are driven by local incomes. In more affordable markets, buyers can accumulate a down payment much faster because home prices—and therefore down payment requirements—are significantly lower,” Chen Zhao, Redfin Head of Economic Research, said in a statement released with Rocket Mortgage’s findings.

Some cities are responding with childcare initiatives, but experts say it isn’t clear whether the policies will make a big enough impact.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is working on a free childcare pilot where about 40 kids of city workers, ages six weeks to three years, will receive year-round childcare during work hours at no cost to the parents. But his campaign promise of universal child care in the Big Apple still has a long way to go.

There are some big cities where the population of kids is growing.

Of the 38 cities with more than 500,000 residents that the WSJ analyzed, 13 saw a seven percent increase in children over the past decade while their overall population grew 12 percent.

Many of those cities were in the Sunbelt and are often affordable for middle-class families, the publication noted.

Andy Burnham is set to unveil the biggest overhaul in education in 15 years with an end to a system which prioritises preparing children for university at the expense of technical training.

The prime minister is to announce the changes as part of a new drive to tackle “a lost generation” with 1 million young people unemployed or trapped outside education.

It comes after he revealed to the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg that he plans to bring down the welfare bill by making benefits conditional on people finding work, especially ones linked to mental health issues such as anxiety and stress.

But the move to value “the hard hat as much as the graduation cap” is another break with former Labour prime minister Sir Tony Blair’s legacy, which saw vocational qualifications downgraded in favour of getting 50 per cent of school leavers to university.

Ahead of the announcement, Mr Burnham said: “For too long in this country, students have been told that you must take the academic path to do well and to be respected. The whole school system has been built around it and that has let down young people seeking technical qualifications.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham is set to announce major education reform ( AFP/Getty )

“I want an education system based on parity between academic and technical which gives all young people a clear path in life. From today, Britain will value the hard hat every bit as much as the graduation cap.”

He added: “Fixing the youth unemployment crisis in Britain will require a major shake-up in how we do things – and that’s what this government will do. I want to ensure that our education system leaves no dead ends for our young people. The changes we’re announcing today will just be the start of our work to restore opportunity and hope across the country.”

It represents the biggest shift in education since Michael Gove rolled out the school academies and free school reforms in 2011.

But the focus on vocational qualifications also comes at a time when graduates are being hit with massive levels of debt from paying for tuition fees while many are struggling to find employment.

The new pathways of prestigious technical routes will provide 14-year-olds with early access to technical skills, work experience and connections with local employers.

Mr Burnham believes that funding for the changes will come the existing £570m investment to create additional college places across the country, alongside the wider Department for Education settlement agreed at the 2025 Spending Review, which increased schools funding by £4.7bn by 2028-29.

The prime minister has made it clear that he is determined to put technical education on an equal footing with the traditional academic path and to ensure there are “no dead ends” for young people coming out of the education system.

This will mean providing high-quality technical education routes that are valued and respected by students, parents and employers. In a message directly to students, he will say “whether you choose construction, coding or classics, you’ll get the skills you need and be given the respect you deserve”.

Under the plans, from age 14 (Year 10), students will have the chance to combine core academic subjects – including English, maths and science – with technical education linked to jobs available in their area. They will be able to spend time with employers and gain real-world experience.

Mr Burnham believes he will be building on initiatives which he championed as mayor of Manchester, such as the MBacc (Greater Manchester Baccalaureate), and the new technical routes will mean young people can develop the technical knowledge and skills needed to progress in areas like engineering, healthcare and digital technology, skilling them up with the specific knowledge and capabilities that local employers need.

open image in gallery Former health secretary Alan Milburn speaks to the media in late May about his interim report Young People and Work ( PA )

As part of his devolution plans, regional mayors, local leaders, schools, colleges and employers will work together to shape the new technical education pathways, which can be tailored around local industries and growth sectors.

The prime minister will pledge that the government will prioritise funding towards high-quality technical education and practical routes into work. The government will also change the way school performance is measured. Inspectors will recognise the schools that provide high-quality technical education and support young people to develop the skills, experience and confidence employers want.

It comes after former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn's interim report warned that Britain is at risk of a "lost generation", with over a million 16- to 24-year-olds now not in education, employment or training.

His findings painted a stark picture of a system that too often leaves young people leaving school without the skills, experience or connections they need to step into the world of work.

Mr Milburn said: “The changes the PM is announcing today are very welcome. They are a big step in the right direction and consistent with the findings of my review. A whole system reset is needed across health, welfare and labour market policy as well as in education and skills.”

The move has also been welcomed by business leaders and trade unions. Michelle Ovens, chief executive of Small Business Britain, said: “This is a great step towards preparing young people for the future, which needs to include business skills and entrepreneurship as core to the changing world of work.”

TUC general secretary Paul Nowak said: “Putting technical education on an equal footing with academia brings us closer to the international standard for skills.”

But Tory shadow education secretary Laura Trott said: “The announcements today don’t come anywhere close to undoing the damage Labour has already done to the job market.

“Labour's policies are driving youth unemployment to record highs. They are making it too expensive to hire young people, and destroying jobs with their Jobs Tax and employer red tape. When it's easier for young people to claim benefits than get a job, it's no wonder youth unemployment is rocketing.”

McFly have started working on a new album, a member of the pop punk group has revealed.

The record will be the band’s first album since 2023’s Power To Play, with singer and guitarist Danny Jones saying he wants the group to sound like a “glorified pub band” on it.

Jones said: “It’s all under wraps until I tell you that we’re making a new album.

“We’re in the studio at the minute, and it’s funny because we were just talking about capturing the energy of (performing in a pub), we called ourselves the other day a glorified pub band, that’s what we want to sound like.

“We want to sound like a glorified pub band, but that hopefully can play arenas.”

Jones, 40, said the record would be partly inspired by the recently reunited Oasis, whose catalogue he said was made up of the “biggest sing-along songs ever created”.

open image in gallery Danny Jones won I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here ( ITV )

The former I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! winner added: “We (the public) all feel like we could probably be in Oasis, and I love that, that’s what’s great.

“That’s what was good about punk music, punk music was massive because everybody felt like they could do it…

“Not everybody can sing like Mariah Carey or Whitney Houston, that’s like whoa, that’s god-like…

“So what we’ve been trying to create, actually, we’ve been trying to find ourselves as a band recently, like what will fulfil all four of us, not just one or two of us.

“Because over the years, I feel like maybe we’ve tried to fulfil one of us more than the others, and what we discovered on our last album, there’s been a couple of albums, (Radio:Active) and Power To Play. And when we play those songs, we look at each other and we’re laughing and we’re thinking this is badass, this is awesome.

“We feel amazing, the others are all a little bit more challenging because they’re a bit more poppier or they’re a bit more produced.”

open image in gallery Liam and Noel Gallagher of Oasis, as the teaser trailer for Steven Knight´s upcoming Oasis documentary ( PA )

Formed in 2003, McFly are completed by singer and guitarist Tom Fletcher, bass player Dougie Poynter and drummer Harry Judd.

They have achieved 19 UK top 10 singles including seven number ones, as well as seven top 10 albums including two number ones in Room On The 3rd Floor and Wonderland.

McFly’s best-known songs include 5 Colours In Her Hair, All About You and I’ll Be Ok.

The interview comes as Jones fronts pub chain Greene King’s Live At Your Local campaign, which celebrates grassroots music with 1,000 free gigs and live music events across its venues in August and September, allowing music fans to see emerging talent in their local pubs.

Equalities minister Bridget Phillipson has been appointed Labour Party chairwoman by Andy Burnham, who has tasked her with driving a "culture change" within the party.

Mr Burnham emphasised that Ms Phillipson would ensure Labour remains focused on "delivering for working people".

Her remit includes preparing the party for the next general election, modernising its digital campaigning and establishing the organisation, infrastructure and policy platform vital for electoral success.

Announcing her appointment, Mr Burnham said: "Bridget Phillipson, as party chair, will help drive the culture change our party needs, working alongside Lucy Powell and me to ensure Labour remains focused on delivering for working people.

Ms Phillipson served as Education Secretary under Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership ( UK Parliament )

“She will play a vital role in ensuring the Labour Party is match fit for the next election.

“I am delighted Bridget has accepted this role and I look forward to working closely with her on this vital task.”

Ms Phillipson, who served as Education Secretary under Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership, said: “I am honoured to take on the role of Labour Party chair, working alongside our Prime Minister to put our Labour values and the voices of our movement at the heart of government.

“By uniting together, we will bring hope back to communities and strengthen British society against those working to divide us.

“With the change Labour in government is delivering and will deliver, we have the chance to write a new chapter for our country, one which brings justice, opportunity and fairness for working people, one which brings back hope that tomorrow can be better than today.”

During her time as education secretary, Phillipson oversaw initiatives including the expansion of free breakfast clubs, changes to school inspections and efforts to tackle rising absenteeism. The Sunderland MP has kept her position as equalities minister while handing the education brief to Lucy Powell.

Deputy Labour leader Lucy Powell said: “I look forward to working with Bridget as we build on the culture change in the party that Andy has made a priority.

“Working together, we will ensure the party continues to lead the way in campaigning, with the strongest ground operation in British politics as we prepare for the next general election.”

The Trump administration is preparing to ramp up funding by hundreds of millions of dollars for programs designed to counter China’s growing influence around the world, after it had put a halt to many of those initiatives last year during a flurry of budget and personnel cuts.

The administration notified Congress late last week that it intends to spend $175.8 million to replace outdated and aging undersea telecommunications cables in the Caribbean and Central America to prevent China from moving in. The Associated Press obtained a copy of the notification on Monday.

The administration has expressed deep concern about China's activities in the Americas, pushing back on Chinese ownership of ports at either end of the Panama Canal, infrastructure projects funded by China's Belt and Road initiative in the region, and Chinese investment in the telecommunications sector.

A State Department official said China’s economic activities in the Western Hemisphere pose risks to U.S. national security and prosperity. The official, who was not authorized to speak publicly to the subject and spoke on condition of anonymity, said China's offerings may seem cheaper but in the end wind up being more expensive due to cost overruns, hidden maintenance fees and poor performance.

The underseas cable funding appears to be part of a broader push to restore support for initiatives aimed at blunting Chinese influence globally that would cost many hundreds of millions of dollars more. That is even as President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping put on a show of cooperation and Xi prepares to visit the U.S. this fall.

US weighs wider spending to counter China globally

The State Department is considering spending nearly half a billion dollars more on programs aimed at China throughout the Western Hemisphere, Africa and Asia, according to an internal State Department document obtained by AP.

“The United States must respond to the CCP’s growing economic, technological, and diplomatic leverage around the world which undermines our national interests,” the document says, using the acronym for the Chinese Communist Party.

Many of those proposed programs are designed to “reclaim diplomatic leverage” through investments in areas where the U.S. had previously been spending money but stopped as the Elon Musk-led Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, carried out deep government budget and personnel cuts last year.

Those cuts, which dismantled the U.S. Agency for International Development and eliminated several hundred diplomatic posts worldwide, also affected previously approved projects, including some aimed at countering China.

A senior U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss future administration plans, confirmed the Trump administration’s intent to boost funding on countering China but could not speak to specifics. The official acknowledged discussions of large-scale projects but said many were still in the discussion phase.

Congress told about undersea cable project to keep China away

The program described to Congress on Friday is called the “Countering CCP Control of Caribbean and Central America Undersea Cables project.”

It will “fund the installation of strategically-selected undersea cable infrastructure” and support foreign governments in partnering with private sector undersea cable installers, according to the notification. The money will “support replacement of outdated undersea telecommunications cables in the Caribbean and Central America region with secure, U.S. and trusted alternatives,” it said.

Even as it pursues the war with Iran and peace efforts in Gaza and Lebanon, the Trump administration has put a focus on the Western Hemisphere, capturing Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro earlier this year, ramping up pressure on Cuba’s socialist government in the months since and imposing severe sanctions on the government in Nicaragua.

Under the new program, funding is anticipated to be given to or in support of undersea cable projects benefiting El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Haiti, the document said. The U.S. has tenuous ties with Nicaragua and would not be working with the government there.

China's embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Other anti-China efforts could focus on cyber and critical minerals

At the same time, the administration has drawn up plans to spend more than $340 million for over 50 specific anti-China projects around the world, including many in the Western Hemisphere, according to the internal State Department document outlining various proposals.

The administration notified Congress in May that it had spent several hundred million dollars in counter-China funding from the 2024 budget that was approved by the Biden administration. However, many other projects funded for 2024 and 2025 had been put on hold.

Among the plans to be resurrected are the creation of security operations centers in Argentina and Belize to monitor Chinese threats to critical infrastructure and cyber platforms throughout the region. Also coming back would be initiatives to protect Ecuador, Jamaica, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay from alleged Chinese attempts to infiltrate port operations and illegally exploit offshore fishing and critical minerals extraction.

More broadly, the proposal, which is still under consideration, would work against Chinese influence in the selection of a successor to the Dalai Lama “by developing proprietary technology to ensure secure communications and information collection.” It also would go after international support for China’s space program and push back against Chinese firms seeking to export surveillance and censorship technology.

The document did not describe the initiatives in detail.

Trump is expected to meet with Xi in September around the time of the annual U.N. General Assembly gathering of world leaders in New York. To prepare for that meeting, Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi last week at a regional security conference in the Philippines.

Trump has oscillated between anger and elation with Xi, whom the U.S. leader has sought to cultivate as an ally even while China pursues goals antithetical to many of his administration's. The ultimate impact of the proposed new programs won't be known for many months or years.

British travellers arriving in Bordeaux on Monday braved the smoke as an “unprecedented” wildfire continued to sweep through southwest France, forcing more than 200,000 people to evacuate.

Firefighters were in a race against time to contain the blaze as it came within nine miles from entry points to the main metropolitan area, with a looming heatwave threatening to exacerbate the spread.

Steve Bray, arriving from London Gatwick, told The Independent that he and his partner, Laura Slade, were spending a couple of nights in the city before heading to a wedding in the south.

“Our government didn’t say anything, the French government didn’t say anything, the flights didn’t say anything and the hotel didn’t say anything,” he said.

They assessed that “the French authorities are on top of it and if it was ‘bad bad bad’, then we wouldn’t have been allowed to fly in the first place”.

open image in gallery Eighty firefighters had been injured tackling the blaze, according to local officials ( AFP/Getty )

“It’s all good. Wasn’t put off at all,” he said, adding: “Overall, can’t complain. We’re on holiday, so haven’t got work tomorrow!”

The British Airways flight heading to Bordeaux from Gatwick on Monday afternoon was held on the apron for nearly three hours due to the fires, waiting for a signal on availability to land.

Passengers aboard the almost full flight were handed water and snacks by patient staff. Vicko Parian, also holidaying in the region for a couple of days, said: “We were a bit nervous about [the fires] but then, the hotel was booked and we couldn’t get a refund so we thought ... If worst comes to worst we can always get a train to Paris and then get a Eurostar.”

James Massip, arriving from Luton, said he spent around half an hour waiting before takeoff. “I live here so I know a few people so to be honest, I’ve just been watching the news,” he said.

Mr Massip said he had been “a little bit nervous”, but “more nervous about the airport shutting” and not being able to get home.

open image in gallery Active wildfires continue to spread through southwest France, laying ruin to homes and forcing thousands of evacuations ( AFP/Getty )

Julien Dijols, who lives north of Bordeaux, said he was returning from holiday in the UK on Monday evening.

He said he lived far from the wildfires and was “not really concerned” about the fires personally. He said they had checked on their flights to make sure they would be able to get home.

There was a smell of smoke in the air at Bordeaux airport on Monday night, and a hotel was providing water and face masks to guests.

The British Foreign Office currently advises people in affected areas, or planning to travel to them, to “follow instructions and updates from local authorities and emergency services at all times”.

Travellers are advised to call 112 if in need of emergency help, and to check with their accommodation or travel provider before travelling.

For information on the wildfires in the southwest, a public information line is open from 09:00 to 17:00, +33 (0)9 70 80 90 40 (select option 1 for Gironde, option 2 for Landes).

More than 220,000 people, including tourists and residents, have been evacuated from areas near Bordeaux since unprecedented fires took hold near the Atlantic coast last week.

French interior minister Laurent Nuñez said the fire had not spread overnight but the danger had not passed.

“It isn't contained. I absolutely do not want to sound reassuring. That is not my intention. We must remain very focused and very determined,” he said.

Mr Nuñez said the fire has burned through 40,000 hectares of land already – nearly twice the area burned by wildfires in the Gironde region in 2022.

Mathilde Sauveroche, a resident of Bordeaux, told The Independent that the fire had given her flashbacks of those of four years ago, until it became clear that the situation now was much worse.

open image in gallery Fires continue to spread across the Gironde region, forcing residents from their homes and jobs ( Esteban de Riberolles )

“On Friday, we started to smell smoke from Bordeaux. By Friday evening the air was unbreathable: itchy throat, eyes stinging,” she said.

“In Cenon on Friday, we also had a tyre workshop that burned down a few streets from my house, so the smell was atrocious.”

She described fleeing the city with her husband over the weekend in search of clean air, before returning this week to work at a daycare centre.

“The drive back was apocalyptic,” she said. “We left under a blue sky and drove through a massive orange-grey cloud. We had stocked up on FFP2 masks to be able to breathe normally. Bordeaux was covered in it.”

open image in gallery French president Emmanuel Macron with interior minister Laurent Nunez, left, in Bordeaux on Monday ( Reuters )

Ms Sauveroche, who works with children, said they have been instructed not to go outside or open windows until the air quality improves.

“We do talk to the kids about the fires so they know what's going on. They can sense the general panic,” she said, adding that they are now asking families to donate baby products where possible.

“What is happening was predicted by scientists so many years ago yet our politicians ignored it. With the French presidential elections coming next year it's even more important people realise the impact it's having on citizens’ lives.”

Temperatures dipped to 32C on Monday, giving firefighters a brief window to try to bring the fire under control. France’s weather office warned that temperatures could rise to 37C later in the week as the heatwave returns.

Eighty firefighters have been injured tackling the blaze, according to local officials. The fires have also forced the evacuation of the entire Cap-Ferret peninsula and several suburbs outside of Bordeaux.

open image in gallery Volunteer firefighters have turned out to help tackle the blaze in areas like Le Porge, where entire homes have been gutted by the wildfires ( AFP/Getty )

Overnight into Sunday, some 55,000 people were evacuated from villages to the south of the city. Many have been evacuated to the Exhibition Centre in Bordeaux, locals said.

Jerome Steffe, mayor of Cestas, a suburb south of Bordeaux, described the blaze as “a fire of a size never seen before”.

French economy minister Roland Lescure told reporters on Monday that more than 13,000 businesses have had to evacuate their premises due to the wildfires so far.

The Independent contacted British Airways for comment

More than half a century passed before some measure of justice was served over the weekend for the murder of popular Chilean singer-songwriter Víctor Jara.

Chilean police on Saturday arrested a retired military colonel who had been a fugitive for three years after being convicted of kidnapping and murdering Jara during Chile’s military dictatorship and sentenced to 25 years in prison.

Despite the arrest, the musician's family says they are not completely satisfied.

“We learned that retired Colonel Nelson Haase Mazzei, who had been a fugitive from justice since 2023, was found and imprisoned. We appreciate this news,” said Jara's daughter, Amanda Jara, in a letter published Sunday night. However, she added, “it is difficult to consider this justice.”

The prominent military figure had been sentenced to 25 years and two days in prison for the kidnapping and murder of Jara and then-Director General of Prisons Littré Quiroga Carvajal.

Haase Mazzei, 80, was convicted in 2018 and his sentence was increased in 2023, along with those of six other military officers. The crimes are considered to be among the most emblematic examples of the brutality that marked the 17-year dictatorship of late Gen. Augusto Pinochet.

The former official fled before beginning his prison term. He was finally located and arrested this weekend — three years later — with Judge Paola Plaza of the Santiago Court of Appeals ordering his “immediate imprisonment,” the Judiciary said in a statement. The institution added that Haase Mazzei was the last of those convicted to begin serving his sentence.

One of the symbols of the so-called New Chilean Song, a musical and social movement born in the 1960s, Jara was murdered on Sept. 16, 1973, just five days after the coup that overthrew former President Salvador Allende.

Jara, then a 40-year-old member of the Communist Party of Chile who also worked as a professor at the State Technical University, was arrested on campus and taken to Chile Stadium, now renamed Víctor Jara Stadium. There, he was separated from the nearly 5,000 other prisoners and taken to a private area. Along with Quiroga, he was tortured, violently assaulted and finally executed. The singer suffered multiple fractures and his body had 44 bullet wounds, according to the findings of an investigation into his death and other crimes of the period.

In 1991, months after Pinochet’s downfall and the restoration of democracy, an official report by the National Commission for Truth and Reconciliation found that Jara was the victim of a political execution and classified his killing as a grave human rights violation. It also found that, in just three months, 890 people were killed as a direct consequence of the military coup.

In recent decades, Chile has established a series of truth commissions to investigate and determine responsibility for the violations committed between 1973 and 1990, ranging from murders and torture to forced disappearances and the illegal adoption of children.

Official documents estimate that during its 17 years, the military dictatorship left some 40,000 victims, including more than 2,000 people who were executed, 1,469 victims of enforced disappearance and thousands more tortured. The courts have convicted hundreds of state agents and civilians for the crimes committed during the darkest period of Chile's modern history. However, there are no single, consolidated institutional figures that include all those sentenced.

Since 2024, the country has also promoted the so-called National Search Plan aimed at unifying the figures and outlining a road map for the search of disappeared detainees whose whereabouts remain unknown — a task that for years has largely fallen to the families of victims who to this date are still trying to figure out what happened with their loved ones.

“We hope that the police will manage to find all those who fled for crimes against humanity,” Amanda Jara concluded in her letter. She now heads the Víctor Jara Foundation.

News.title: Human first, athlete second: Ramsay-Peaty finds peace despite second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

News.title: Is equity release a good idea? Pros and cons
News.content:
How safe is equity release?

When weighing up the pros and cons, one of your biggest questions might be whether equity release is safe. There are several myths about equity release, so this is a common concern.

You should make sure that any company or adviser you are dealing with is a member of the Equity Release Council. This is the industry trade body that sets standards for equity release products. Royal London Equity Release Advisers, the provider of the Telegraph Media Group Equity Release Service, is a member of the Equity Release Council.

Considerations can vary depending on the product you choose, whether that is a lifetime mortgage or a home reversion plan.

This article will focus on the pros and cons of lifetime mortgages, the most popular equity release product.

News.title: Amazon has ended support for pre-2013 Kindles. What to do if you’re affected (and what to avoid)
News.content:
It seems like a lot of devices, but Amazon told Engadget that the move will affect around three per cent of current users. In theory, if you’re using a device that’s affected, then Amazon should already have notified you via email. If in doubt, however, the company has a support page with pictures and specifications of every Kindle ever released. If you’re still unsure, entering the model number into Google should reveal the exact version you’re using. This can typically be found on the back of devices.

For Kindle Fire tablets, the process is simpler. Open the Settings menu and select “Device Options”. You’ll find the model you’re using either under “Device Model” or “About Fire Tablet”.

Why did this happen?

Nobody expects electronic devices to be supported forever, but it’s disappointing that the Kindle’s most enthusiastic early adopters got cut off. Given the basic functionality of e-book reader technology, there doesn’t appear to be a technical reason behind the decision, making it appear like an anti-consumer move to push older customers towards the purchase of newer devices where existing Kindles would become an e-waste casualty.

When asked why these devices were losing support, we received a response defending the (admittedly impressive) longevity.

“These models have been supported for at least 14 years – some as long as 18 years – but technology has come a long way in that time, and these devices will no longer be supported moving forward,” an Amazon spokesperson said. “We are notifying those still actively using them and offering promotions to help with the transition to newer devices.”

At the initial time of writing, the promotions mentioned appeared to be 20 per cent off “select new Kindle devices” alongside a £15 eBook credit. While the latter was welcome, the highlighted discount is somewhat disappointing for a number of reasons. Firstly, according to the promotion’s terms and conditions, the “select” caveat excludes the most expensive model, the Kindle Scribe. It doesn’t apply to Fire devices for those tablet owners looking to replace like-for-like, either.

More importantly, the prices aren’t all that impressive considering happy owners of older Kindles weren’t budgeting for this purchase. Amazon frequently discounts its own-brand devices like Echo smart speakers and Fire tablets, and 20 per cent isn’t that unusual. Last year’s Black Friday sale saw discounts of over 30 per cent on the basic Kindle and Kindle Colorsoft, and the price-tracking site CamelCamelCamel shows that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition has been as low as £183 in the past – a 32 per cent discount on its current price of £269.

There was added time pressure, too. Amazon said the discount and credit offer was only valid until June 20, one month after support for the older Kindles ended.

Additionally, owners of the earliest UK Kindle will see that prices have gone up over the past decade. The £109 they paid in 2010 is some way off the £159.99 Kindle Paperwhite, even with a 20 per cent discount, let alone the £219.99 Kindle Colorsoft. That said, at £94.99, the basic Kindle 12th Generation remains a bargain for no-frills readers, with a 20 per cent discount taking it down to £75.99.

Possible upgrades

If you’re affected by this news, the silver lining is that while e-book technology moves relatively slowly, things have still advanced significantly in the past 14 years. Resolutions are higher; most are backlit for bedtime reading; there’s support for audiobooks; and storage has increased. There are also optional extras like colour screens, blue-light filters to prevent eye strain and waterproofing.

As outlined in our guide to the best Kindles, our pick for most people is the 12th Generation Kindle Paperwhite, which costs £159.99 with lockscreen ads or £169.99 without. The seven inch screen with warm lighting makes for a comfortable reading experience, and it’s waterproof for bathtime or poolside reading.

At £94.99 (or £104.99 without ads), the basic 11th Generation Kindle is a great budget pick, however. It’s slightly smaller at six inches, and like the Paperwhite, can hold around 8,000 e-books with support for audiobooks through Audible. It lacks the warm light and waterproofing, however, and its battery life is around half that of the Paperwhite — albeit still a generous six weeks of normal use.

The two remaining Kindles occupy specific niches. The Kindle Colorsoft has a colour screen, making it well suited to those who enjoy graphic novels. The Kindle Scribe, meanwhile, has a bundled stylus for note taking.

Can I still use my old Kindle?

Yes, Amazon said users would be able to “continue to read books already downloaded on these devices”. If you factory reset your older Kindle, however, or you deregister it, you won’t be able to use it anymore.

News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

Sports.content:
Yan Diomande, Vinicius Jr and Bradley Barcola are in the headlines this summer

The latest transfer news, including updates on Arsenal's interest in Vinicius Junior, Liverpool working to complete a deal for Bradley Barcola and Real Madrid's agreement with Yan Diomande

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Monday, July 27.

The big news from the weekend is Arsenal’s interest in Vinicius Junior. The Daily Telegraph is reporting that the Gunners are prepared to offer the Real Madrid star the biggest contract in the club’s history.

The report states that Vinicius currently earns a weekly salary of £400,000, but Arsenal would seek to enhance those terms to increase their chances of executing a bold coup.

Meanwhile, according to the Daily Mail, Liverpool are working to reach an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over Bradley Barcola amid escalating valuations. Real Madrid, meanwhile, have verbally agreed on personal terms with Yan Diomande, according to Sky Germany. Paris Saint-Germain also reportedly reached a deal with him last month, but the Spanish side are now said to be in pole position.

Over in Italy, La Gazzetta dello Sport claims Manchester United are offering Marcus Rashford to Roma in an attempt to reduce the transfer fee for Manu Kone. However, the sports newspaper describes any deal as unlikely due to the player's £325,000-a-week wages.

Sports.title: PSG attack Real Madrid in fresh Yan Diomande transfer statement after ending interest
Sports.content:
PSG attack Real Madrid in fresh Yan Diomande transfer statement after ending interest

Paris Saint-Germain confirmed over the weekend that they've ended their pursuit of RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande, and have now issued a fresh statement taking aim at Real Madrid

View 2 Images Yan Diomande is set to join Real Madrid (Image: Stacy Revere/Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain have launched an attack on Real Madrid in fresh comments regarding their former transfer target, Yan Diomande. PSG announced on Sunday that they're no longer interested in the 19-year-old, who RB Leipzig will demand at least £100million for after turning down an £85m bid from Real last week.

‌



But the French and European champions haven't stopped there. On Monday, PSG claimed via French newspaper L'Equipe that the 'crazy money' which Real could end up paying for the Ivory Coast international 'shows where they are right now'.

‌



The club said: "They were asking for crazy money for a player who has potential but was playing in the Spanish second division one year ago. We won't break the bank because a club arrived with fireworks.

‌



Sticking the knife in, PSG added: "This shows where Real Madrid are right now."

Diomande moved to Leipzig from Spanish second-tier side Leganes last summer and enjoyed a superb season in Germany. The winger won the Bundesliga's young player of the season award for 2025-26, having scored 12 goals and provided eight assists.

‌



The inter-club drama comes after PSG stated that they would 'not break its principals' by bending to Leipzig's demands. "The asking transfer fee and salary demands were completely disproportionate and distortive - and PSG will not break its principles of rational financial management and squad balance," the Ligue 1 side said.

"As a two-time consecutive Champions League winner and the most successful club in recent years, PSG will also not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents - and will instead calmly and confidently continue its transfer planning."

How much is Yan Diomande worth? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Paris Saint-Germain have abandoned a move for Yan Diomande (Image: Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Diomande was also a target for Liverpool, but it appears that Real are the clear frontrunners. His arrival could have a knock-on effect for the future of Vinicius Junior.

Arsenal are keen on Vinicius, who's entered the final year of his £400,000-a-week contract with Real, who will be due to pay him a significant loyalty bonus if he stays put for the 2026-27 season. The Brazilian didn't return to training on Monday as previously planned amid growing uncertainty over his future.

Article continues below

Should Real decided to sell him, Arsenal are prepared to hand him a lucrative deal that would increase his salary. New Real manager Jose Mourinho, however, doesn't want to lose Vinicius just weeks into his second spell in the Bernabeu dugout.

Sports.title: Lionel Scaloni pleads with Argentina fans as he is blocked from seeing DENTIST
Sports.content:
Lionel Scaloni pleads with Argentina fans as he is blocked from seeing DENTIST

Lionel Scaloni has returned home after guiding Argentina to the World Cup final, where his team surrendered their grip on the trophy and were beaten 1-0 by Spain in extra-time

View Image Lionel Scaloni was mobbed by fans

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni had to plead with fans blocking his way to the DENTIST after returning home from the World Cup. Scaloni's side suffered heartbreak in last Sunday's final when they lost 1-0 to Spain in extra-time.

‌



Argentina came into this summer's World Cup among the favourites, having won their last three tournaments under Scaloni. But Ferran Torres' late goal saw the trophy go to Spain, who dominated the final in New Jersey.

‌



But the 48-year-old still came home to a hero's welcome. Supporters have even been camping on his garden lawn in the town of Pujato, close to Rosario.

‌



Footage from a video which has gone viral shows Scaloni attempting to make his way through the adoring fans while security usher him to a car. The former West Ham defender gave high-fives to some children, while adults tried having a moment with their beloved boss.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Spain star Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of lying after World Cup final brawl READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

"I have a dentist appointment," he can heard telling the crowd. "I will be back soon."

‌



Scaloni has now left Pujato, with his family having to put a note on the door after fans continued to turn up. "Leo left last night!!! Thanks for all the love."

In a classy move, Scalno is said have come out of his house every afternoon to greet them. The Albiceleste manager signed autographs and posed for selfies with supporters of all ages.

Football fans on social media have been stunned by the warm reception. "It's as though they won the World Cup. Massive love," one posted on X.

‌



What do you make of Argentina's performance at the World Cup? Have your say in the comments section.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"Best manager in their history," another concluded on Reddit. A third said: "Nice guy for doing all that for the fans. It seems overwhelming though, to have so many people surrounding him all the time."

‌



One user agreed and wrote: "Bro literally can't go home without being hounded. That's gotta feel insane."

It's been an emotional eight days for Scaloni, who lifted the World Cup four years ago to earn himself immortality in his homeland. This year's final didn't go their way and Scaloni broke down in tears during his post-match press conference.

He posted a statement via Instagram on Monday, writing: "After an intense week where sadness intertwined with joy, tears with smiles, anguish with tranquillity, and nerves with calm, I can finally sit down to write a few words. Although you know I'm not big on social media, it might be the best way to get this message to you.

‌



"All I can say is I'm sorry I couldn't bring home another trophy and give you a new reason to celebrate - something that, even if only for a few days, might have made you forget life's hardships.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"But I want you to focus on what we tried to show you through this group of players - my warriors, as I called them when speaking about them to my wife. The effort, the drive, the desire, the 'I can do it' attitude, refusing to give up (even when the odds are stacked against you).

‌



"Giving your all (even when you have nothing left), weathering the cold showers of criticism (FROM PEOPLE WHO DON'T KNOW US), maintaining composure. And finding the will to stay on your feet when your legs no longer obey your brain…That is the true trophy.

"I am eternally grateful to my coaching staff, the players, the AFA staff - those who work quietly behind the scenes to ensure our comfort - and to each and every one of you for the affection you've shown us.

"P.S. Whoever has an Argentine friend has a treasure."

Sports.title: John Stones decides next club after England star holds talks with Chelsea
Sports.content:
John Stones decides next club after England star holds talks with Chelsea

John Stones is eyeing his next club after leaving Manchester City at the end of the season and, despite talks with Chelsea, has decided on his next move

View 2 Images John Stones has turned down the chance to sign for Chelsea

John Stones has decided to move abroad following his Manchester City exit despite holding talks with Chelsea over a possible switch.

‌



The England centre-half has just called time on his decade at the Etihad, which saw him win the Premier League on six occasions as well as the Champions League. The 32-year-old remains a strong performer and wasn't shy of suitors this summer.

‌



Chelsea were keen to add his quality and experience to their ranks with Xabi Alonso now in charge and multiple rounds of talks were held with the Blues. Ultimately Stones rejected the prospect of a move to Stamford Bridge to pursue his ambitions of playing elsewhere in Europe.

‌



Stones has played for Barnsley, Everton and City but is now closing in on a move to Inter Milan, according to reports. An agreement in principle has been secured with the Englishman, who has agreed on a deal until 2028.

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing READ MORE :

Inter will go into the campaign as defending champions having won Serie A, their second Italian title in the last three years. They currently boast no English players in their ranks but a move to the San Siro would allow Stones to reignite his relationship with Manuel Akanji, whom he played with at City.

‌



Another Three Lions defender in Fikayo Tomori is playing at city rivals AC Milan, where he's been since 2021, although he is being linked with a move away.

Stones will bring the ball-playing ability that first attracted Pep Guardiola, who encouraged him to adopt more of a midfield role during his time in Manchester.

View 2 Images Inter Milan are poised to add the England defender

Article continues below

The veteran defender spoke in glowing terms about his time in Manchester, where he helped the club enjoyed their most successful period ever. He said: “It’s been a roller coaster. You can look at it like that and everything has ups and downs and good things, bad things. But to live out all my dreams and all my goals and all the things that I set out to achieve as a player and live as a player.

“Doing that has just been a dream and to be able to give that to everyone and do it in the style and fashion that we have and make everyone’s dream come true with obviously that Treble season, something that the club’s never achieved or won. It’s been so special.”

Sports.title: Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked
Sports.content:
Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked

Paolo Maldini has reportedly quit as Italy's technical director after just over two weeks in the role following the decision to block Andrea Pirlo from becoming manager

View 2 Images Paolo Maldini has quit his role with Italy

Italy's technical director Paolo Maldini has quit after only 16 days having seen Andrea Pirlo blocked for the vacant manager's role, according to reports.

‌



The Azzurri are on the lookout for a new boss after Gennaro Gattuso quit following another failure to qualify for the World Cup. As part of a huge reset Maldini, who played his entire career at AC Milan and won 126 caps for his country, was hired into a senior role.

‌



He was tasked with restoring Italy to their former glory and the all-time great defender had pushed for Pirlo’s appointment. After seeing that request turned down Sky Italy claim he has now walked away after just over two weeks in his job.

‌



Pirlo, part of the victorious 2006 World Cup side, expressed his frustration at being snubbed with a post on social media. He wrote: "After learning last night that I am no longer the candidate to lead the Italian national team, I believe it is my duty to clarify a few points.

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

"In the last few days I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking over the role of head coach of the Italian national team.

Pirlo was not allowed to take on the role because of his connections to the Russian betting company Fonbet, where he is a brand ambassador. The former player has said it is “strictly commercial and sporting in nature”. Some involved in the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), as well as politicians, didn't think it was right he took up the post due to the ongoing war in Ukraine.

‌



Pirlo is ultimately the third major name to miss out on the role. Pep Guardiola said no for personal reasons and Carlo Ancelotti didn't want to leave his gig with Brazil.

View 2 Images Andrea Pirlo was overlooked for the role due to ties with Russia (Image: Gabriele Siri/IPA Sport/ipa-agency.net/REX/Shutterstock)

Gattuso resigned in April after Italy’s failure to qualify for this summer’s World Cup. They finished below Norway in qualifying and then lost to Bosnia-Herzegovina on penalties in the play-offs.

Article continues below

It further amplified Italy's decline with the Azzurri now missing out on the 2018, 2022 and 2026 editions. They became the first winner in history to fail to qualify for three tournaments on the bounce as their Euros success of five years ago continues to look like a distant memory.

Italy came into those championships off the back of a sensational unbeaten run and downed the likes of Belgium and Spain before beating England at Wembley in the final. Roberto Mancini was their manager but, despite some high profile men taking the job since, they continue to fall short.

Sports.title: Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing
Sports.content:
Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing

Jordan Henderson is a target for multiple Premier League clubs, with Brentford willing to let him go on a free transfer, and Chelsea are understood to be leading the race for his services

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson is another shock target for Chelsea (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

Chelsea are working on a surprise move for Jordan Henderson, sitting first in the queue of Premier League clubs who are interested in signing him. Henderson, 36, has an agreement which will him to leave Brentford on a free transfer, despite having one year left on his contract.

‌



The midfielder is currently injured after breaking his arm during England's celebrations following their last-16 win against Mexico at the World Cup. Henderson stayed in North America for the rest of the tournament, remaining a key figure within the dressing room.

‌



His leadership and experience are part of why Xabi Alonso wants to bring him to Stamford Bridge. The Athletic report that Chelsea are the leading contenders for the former Liverpool captain's signature.

‌



It's added that multiple Premier League clubs also want to sign him. Chelsea's interest comes after they opened talks with Brighton to sign 35-year-old Danny Welbeck, further proof of their change of transfer policy since Alonso was appointed.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Last month, the Blues bid £8m for Granit Xhaka after the Sunderland captain signalled that he'd be willing reunite with Alonso, who he played under at Bayer Leverkusen. Sunderland flatly rejected the offer and Xhaka will stay.

‌



Henderson is seen as alternative, with Alonso wanting an experienced head in midfield, while he also gets on well with Chelsea's new £117million signing, Morgan Rogers. The England international only joined Brentford a year ago from Ajax, previously playing for Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq having left Liverpool in July 2023.

But his impact off the pitch is valued, too. After beating France 6-4 in the World Cup third-place play-off, England boss Thomas Tuchel revealed that the 35-year-old had given a powerful speech pre-match speech which motivated his team-mates.

"Jordan Henderson gave a very impressive speech today in the hotel to put this in the right frame and put everyone in the right mindset," Tuchel explained. "So he helped unbelievably today.

‌



Should Jordan Henderson join Chelsea? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson stayed with the England squad, despite breaking his arm (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

"That was very emotional and very, very impressive to put this game into perspective. I won't say what he said, but it puts into it perspective because he was part of this match eight years ago.

‌



"It was very emotional and he put into perspective what you might feel in the very moment, that you might give in to the feeling 'I don't want to be here'. He took all of that away because he said that it means the world in the end, and he would give anything if he hadn't broken his arm to be part again in this match.

"You never know when you get a World Cup match for England. He said it much, much better than me and more emotional, and it was very impressive. He set the tone and the mindset for this match."

Man Utd star takes drastic action as Ruben Amorim plots transfer reunion

One Manchester United player could be set for a departure from Old Trafford and a reunion with a former boss in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Manchester United star Noussair Mazraoui has been linked with a reunion with Ruben Amorim (Image: (Photo by Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Manchester United defender Noussair Mazraoui has reportedly switched agents as speculation continues to mount regarding a potential departure from Old Trafford. Reports earlier this summer suggested new AC Milan manager and former United boss Ruben Amorim was interested in reuniting with the Morocco international.

‌



The Serie A outfit is searching for a wing-back to feature in Amorim's favoured 3-4-3 system, with Mazraoui being considered. Italian reports indicate the Serie A side would pursue a deal for the United defender, provided decision-makers at Old Trafford signal their willingness to sell.

‌



Amorim had previously heaped praise on Mazraoui during his Old Trafford tenure, saying: "He’s a top player. He understands the game. He knows how to attack, he’s very technical, he’s very good defensively and he’s very good one-on-one."

‌



There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.
