There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.

‌



Amorim, speaking in December 2024, added: "He’s a modern player. I think he’s the future of our team. When you think about him, you think we need more players like Nous that can control the tempo, they are really, really good and comfortable with the ball. So, Nous, I’m really happy with him."

The Moroccan defender was a regular for his country as they reached the latter stages of the World Cup, just a few months on from reaching the African Cup of Nations final. The 28-year-old defender made 20 appearances for United last season, sitting out a substantial portion of the campaign for the African Cup of Nations.

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim could raid his former club (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Mazraoui found it difficult to regain his spot in Michael Carrick's team after coming back from the winter competition, but did catch the eye of the then-interim United manager, eventually reclaiming his place in the starting XI.

"Yeah he's come back well, Nous," Carrick said last season after reintegrating Mazraoui back into the side. "It was a difficult one, obviously, on the back of the final and how it panned out.

"[He had] a few days to digest that then back in and around it. He's been fantastic in and around the group and around training.

Article continues below

"Obviously, he came on at the end of the game and played a part for us, as you'd expect. So yeah, again [we want to] just keep thickening the squad, bolstering the squad and it's great to have him back."

Sports.title: Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies
Sports.content:
Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies

Benjamin Sesko continues to edge towards full fitness after missing Manchester United's early pre-season friendlies and is on target to play in their Premier League opener

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko is on course to be fit for the start of the Premier League

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko is on course to be fit before the Premier League season starts despite missing successive pre-season friendlies.

‌



The Slovenian has been struggling with a shin injury and that meant he was absent for games against Wrexham and Rosenborg as he continues to follow a rehabilitation program. Sesko was already nursing a shin injury that he aggravated in the win over Liverpool in early May.

‌



United kept their cards close to their chest regarding the extent of the injury at the time as the striker missed the last three games of the campaign having been a regular up until then.

‌



However, The Sun reports that Sesko’s recovery is going to plan and he was never scheduled to participate in their opening two friendlies.

7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

The ex-RB Leipzig man began outdoor training last week and has a chance of being involved against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on Saturday as he bids to build on what was an impressive debut season, despite a slow start leading to some doubts over his signing.

‌



Sesko is likely to start against PSG in Gothenburg on August 8 before the entire United squad fly from Sweden to Dublin for a six-day training camp. The Red Devils play Leeds at Croke Park on August 12.

United begin their Premier League season against Hull City on August 22 as Michael Carrick prepares for his first full season in charge following a stellar spell in the dugout as an interim, with his results ultimately landing him the job permanently. Sesko's goals proved crucial to their run of 12 wins in 17 games.

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko's last game was the win over Liverpool, where he aggravated an injury (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The Slovenian became a super sub in Carrick's early days, coming off the bench to score the winner against Fulham and then Everton a few weeks later. In between that he scored a stoppage-time leveller at West Ham. Sesko also scored crucial goals in wins over Crystal Palace, Brentford and Liverpool as he ended his debut campaign with 12 goals.

His injury absence has allowed Joshua Zirkzee to start in the recently friendlies, despite United’s preference to sell him. The Dutchman was signed by Erik ten Hag but has struggled to live up to expectations and is very much a squad player. Zirkzee is linked with a return to Italy, but the club need to find a buyer at the right price.

Sports.title: Brundle's verdict on 'relentless' Norris, Piastri-Sainz incident and Malaysia return
Sports.content:
The Hungarian Grand Prix was an entertaining way to finish the first part of the 2026 F1 season before the summer break. The top four or five runners were often all visible in the same camera shot, and that included drivers from all four front running teams.

Lando Norris was on brilliant form and took both pole position and the victory, but not without a serious fight in both respects. It wasn't one of those days where a driver leads every lap from pole position and takes fastest lap. Oscar Piastri seized the lead in the second corner of the race, and Charles Leclerc in his Ferrari secured fastest lap but could only muster a fourth-place finish, and that would have been fifth had Lewis Hamilton in the sister Ferrari not attracted yet another penalty, this time for speeding in the pit-lane by 0.1kph.

It turns out Lewis did release the speed limiter a fraction early in order to beat Kimi Antonelli, who was on track, to the all-important safety car line which crosses the entire track and which decides who has the right to be in front, the driver exiting the pits, or the driver on track. It was declared that Antonelli was there a fraction earlier, and so Hamilton had to yield anyway. It was a pivotal moment for the final podium place and therefore the decision that speeding in the pitlane was a potentially competitive advantage was correct, however small the margin.

Relentless Norris and unfortunate Piastri

Norris was on the radio saying that he was faster than team-mate Piastri in the lead, without specifically asking to be let through. Then he asked to pit first, but the pit wall rightly denied that as team protocol is that the leading of the two drivers has first option on stopping.

It was beginning to look like Norris' slide wide in Turn 2 and handing the lead to Piastri would cost him a victory. McLaren pitted Piastri on Lap 16 to cover off the pit stops from Hamilton and Verstappen, and Norris next lap around on Lap 17.

But it was the second round of stops on this high tyre wear circuit that made the difference. Piastri pitted on Lap 33 again to cover Hamilton on fresh tyres, and then Norris had his chance to prove he was indeed faster by running hard and pitting on Lap 39, giving him a decent tyre life offset to his team-mate Piastri.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

Through the latter stages of the race lapped drivers appeared to be slow or even reluctant to clear the way for the leaders coming through, and it turns out there was an issue with the blue light warning system. That does still leave mirrors and team radio though.

On that same Lap 39, Piastri was coming up to lap Carlos Sainz's Williams who was having his own battle with fellow countryman Fernando Alonso, and after running wide in the infamous Turn 2 which had given Piastri the lead on the opening lap, and which must have looked for all the world to Piastri that he'd seen him and was letting him through, just as Sainz swung heavily back to the racing line and clashed with the race leader.

Sainz had been informed by his Williams team but his position on the outside of a 180 degree turn meant he had no mirror sight of Piastri tight on the inside, and so his penalty was mitigated down to five seconds, which was zero comfort to a rightly angry Piastri.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri was livid after Carlos Sainz makes contact with him in Hungary

Piastri did well not to spin out but he lost crucial time and Norris would emerge from the pits into a lead he would not relinquish. In fact, he would relentlessly increase it despite a third stop under a Virtual Safety Car for fresher soft compound tyres on Lap 56 to recover, so painfully, Piastri's McLaren which had suffered transmission failure.

The young Australian hasn't been able to catch any kind of lucky break for the best part of a year now.

Verstappen fights off Ferraris

Max Verstappen spent much of the race complaining about aerodynamic degradation, poor handling, and inconsistent gear shifting with his Red Bull, but would finish in a fine second place after some impressive overtakes on Hamilton's Ferrari. Max thought Lewis was a bit tough on him in the braking zone, but he wasn't.

It was explained to me that if the Red Bull has any damage on the aero parts particularly underneath the car, on an aggressive kerb for example, this has a disproportionate affect on the overall downforce and so grip. Hence Max's aero degradation comment.

Ferrari had looked the team to beat throughout practice, and most folk in the paddock thought they were favourites even though Norris pipped them to pole. Hamilton had smartly saved a brand new set of soft tyres by clearing the first stage of qualifying on medium tyres. These would have been extremely handy from his front-row grid slot, but he attracted a three-place grid drop from a rather brutal but unintentional blocking of another driver who was on his final qualifying attempt. You'll not be surprised to read the blocked driver was Piastri.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Leclerc fluffed his qualifying with a delete lap time for track limits, and had only managed to save a set of lightly used soft tyres to start the race with. You may remember that Ferrari humbled the entire pack from the start down to the first corner in the earlier races of the season, but such is the development curve in this business, even with a tyre advantage, Hamilton only made up one place on the opening lap and Leclerc, starting on the right hand and dirtier side of the grid, fell from the front row to fifth. And now they had to manage those soft tyres and following other cars, and so their race was immediately compromised.

Ferrari would try to help Hamilton with relatively early stops on Laps 13 and 30 for the speed of fresh tyres. But with Verstappen's combative prowess this paid no dividends. Ferrari pitted both drivers again under the Lap 56 Virtual Safety Car for fresher soft tyres but that only served to allow Antonelli to get ahead (as explained earlier), a position he would keep to the final podium spot.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton responds to his speeding penalty from the Hungarian Grand Prix

Mercedes curiously off the pace

Having dominated this season so far, Mercedes were curiously off the ultimate pace, and a three-place grid penalty for Antonelli for failing to sufficiently lift for yellow warning flags in qualifying when Verstappen spun in the final corner, meant that he had lined up seventh, one place behind team-mate George Russell who was also struggling for pace.

George had also collected some engine damage with a run over the kerbs in Turn 4 and would need a new power unit fitted for race day. Whether all this new kit was responsible for a truly awful start is not so far certain, but Toto Wolff seemed clear it was a car issue.

Everything on a racing car, and especially a Formula 1 car, is positioned as low as absolutely possible to lower the centre of gravity, and so helping the handling through corners, and this leaves components vulnerable.

Russell would drop all the way back to 21st and begin a long afternoon fighting back to seventh place, tantalisingly close to Isack Hadjar's Red Bull in sixth.

Antonelli would secure that podium to increase his championship lead to 50 points over Hamilton heading into the break, and 59 points over his team-mate Russell. That's very much the definition of 'damage limitation' from seventh on the grid in such a competitive field on a circuit notoriously difficult for overtaking.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell and Kimi Antonelli react to their respective seventh and third place finishes at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Liam Lawson would finish a fine eighth and Arvid Lindblad 10th for Racing Bulls to move them up into a fifth in the Constructors' Championship ahead of Alpine. What a happy and cohesive team that appears to be.

And Nico Hulkenberg scored two points for Audi in ninth. In my mind's eye, so far this season I think of Audi consistently around and inside the top ten on pace, but actually they are eighth of 11 teams in the championship, underlining that with an improvement in reliability they can be strong contenders in the relentless midfield battle in the second half.

Aston Martin made a decent jump in performance with a comprehensive aero upgrade, and apparently leapfrogging Cadillac and Williams, and threatening Haas, all at once, but they along with Honda still have a long way to go. Nonetheless it was finally encouraging for the Silverstone team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso says Aston Martin’s new upgrades have delivered the improvements they expected, making the car easier to drive, but admits there is still more potential to unlock

Championship far from over

If McLaren have made a decent upgrade step which translates well to other circuits, this was the team's 14th Hungaroring victory, and with the top four are ever closer, this championship is far from over. There are still 291 points available assuming all the remaining races take place given the Middle East conflict.

On that subject, the Bahrain GP will now be run at the very popular Sepang circuit in Malaysia. This is the same impressive lateral thinking and flexibility F1 and its partners showed during the pandemic and I applaud it.

It sounds as if there will definitely be a European replacement race in late November or early December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi can't take place. We may need to fit some headlights and wipers for that race but the teams and drivers will handle it in their stride as usual.

I wish you all a happy summer break.

MB

Sports.title: 'Pressure is on Antonelli' - Norris not ruling out title fightback
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has not ruled out mounting a title fightback and says all the pressure is on Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Norris claimed McLaren's first Grand Prix win of the season on Sunday with an impressive performance at the Hungarian Grand Prix and sits fifth in the Drivers' Championship, 91 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining.

Last year, Max Verstappen was 104 points off the championship lead with 10 events to go and fell just two points short of the title, which was won by Norris.

"The pressure is on him [Antonelli] for sure. There's no pressure on me. I've been feeling very confident," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

"They [Mercedes] have made more mistakes as a team and we have made less and we have come strong but I expect them to still win races and expect us to win more races. We just need to be perfect from here on now for the whole year.

"We need to improve the car still. We were certainly the quickest in Hungary from qualifying to the race. Not every race is going to be this simple, and we are going to be as quick, so we need to work hard to try to get the car to be this good to get the car to be this good everywhere. If we can, maybe that's a genuine question."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

McLaren brought a major upgrade packaged to Hungary, including a new floor, which has given them a big chunk of pace, having been able to fight at the front for most of the season.

Team principal Andrea Stella expects everyone to continue to bring new parts after the summer break, so McLaren must continue to improve too.

"Like it's always been in this 2026 season, it's a matter of a race of upgrades. The good news is that McLaren is now back in this race of upgrades, while fighting for the lead," he said.

"But I expect that the car that will be the best car at the end of the season will keep adding tenths of a second in the next 11 races, probably as much as half a second. So definitely a lot of work ahead of everyone, not only McLaren."

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

Norris defends pit priority call in Hungary

Norris lost out to Piastri on the opening lap of Sunday's race and was stuck behind his team-mate, despite clearly having more pace in hand.

He eventually used that speed advantage around the second pit stop phase by running longer than Piastri and overcutting the Australian. Prior to that moment, Norris wanted to pit first and had stated on the radio he was "miles faster".

"I just want to win the race. There are certain rules we have as a team, and we can't harm each other's race by being overly aggressive and wanting to win," said Norris in the press conference.

"But I want to win, and I certainly had much better pace than him. We had a much better chance of winning the race, let's say.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris reacts to his first win of 2026 saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

"When I was stuck behind Oscar, Max was three or four seconds behind, and at that point he's still a threat. Ahead, there's no threat, and we have a lot more of a guarantee that we'll win as a team anyway.

"So, I wanted to box and undercut because my pace would have been so good, I could have pulled away a whole pit-stop window, I think, on him and boxed again if I needed to. Or I get him to box early. I think we were on the fine line between boxing too early and harming both of our races.

"So, it was just in the best interests of the team, which they rightly have to say back against me. But I want to do whatever I can to try and win a race, of course."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

Norris has generally had the upper hand over Piastri in recent races and many feel the British driver is performing just as well as last year when he became world champion.

The McLaren driver is unsure why his pace advantage was so significant in Hungary but hopes he continues to have the same feelings in the car after the summer break.

"The cars are identical, and I've just been feeling very strong lately. I've worked on many areas from last year," he said.

"I feel much more confident lately with how to extract performance, and I've worked a lot with my engineers to understand this car because it's certainly not an easy car to understand and figure out how to drive on the limit consistently.

"So, why? Just hard work. Hard work from my engineers and from myself to improve me as a driver and improve my driving. That is the answer."

Sports.title: What Arsenal's interest and Real's Diomande pursuit mean for Vini Jr
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior's Real Madrid future has been the subject of recent speculation, with Arsenal exploring a deal for the forward, but what could happen next?

What is the latest on Vinicius Jr?

Brazil star Vinicius Jr, 26, is entering the final year of his contract at Real Madrid.

Negotiations over an extension have dragged on without a breakthrough and it has caused increasing speculation over his future at the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Vinicius Jr's five best Real Madrid goals in LaLiga last season

That intensified last week when it emerged that Arsenal are interested in signing him this summer if he cannot agree a new deal at Real.

Meanwhile, Real Madrid have made a significant move for another winger - the exciting Ivory Coast international Yan Diomande at RB Leipzig.

It means doubts around Vinicius' future at the Bernabeu have grown over the past few days.

How serious is Arsenal's interest and can they afford him?

Arsenal's interest is real but in the early stages and conditional on a number of factors, not least the cost - which would be significant should the door open for Vinicius to leave Real.

There have been no club-to-club talks and there is no guarantee it progresses to a formal bid.

Arsenal, as newly-crowned Premier League champions, are looking to add another top-class forward despite signing Christos Tzolis. He was brought in to replace Leandro Trossard and there is doubt around the future of Gabriel Martinelli.

Last year they were keen on Vinicius's Real Madrid team-mate Rodrygo, while this summer Sky Sports News has reported their interest in Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers, who has since joined Chelsea from Aston Villa.

With one year left on his contract, the financial side of purchasing Vinicius would not be as severe as it previously has been - but it is worth remembering the sheer scale of an offer for the player two years ago from the Saudi Pro League.

Image: Vinicius Jr's stats from last season at Real Madrid

They were ready to pay him €1bn over five years and a transfer fee to Real Madrid of more than £300m (around €350m), which would have made him the most expensive transfer in history.

It would not cost anywhere near that much this time, but it gives a sense of what both Real and Vinicius were willing to forego in 2024.

Although the exact figure is confidential, Vinicius is believed to earn between €15m and €17m net per year. That's around £247,000 to £279,000 per week after tax. To earn that amount in the UK, Arsenal would need to pay him somewhere between £450,000 and £500,000 per week.

That would make him Arsenal's highest-paid player by far. Bukayo Saka is widely believed to be the current highest-paid, earning more than £300,000 per week.

A report in The Telegraph this morning claims Arsenal would be willing to go to £400,000. But that would still not equal Vinicius' current salary. Widespread reports in Spain claim that part of the current impasse with Real stems from his increased salary demands.

So is it just a dispute over a new contract?

Image: Vinicius Junior celebrates after scoring for Real Madrid in last season's Champions League clash with Manchester City at the Etihad

The situation has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest, further talks to come.

But there is no strong public evidence yet that Vinicius wants to leave Real Madrid for any reason, sporting or otherwise; no quotes, no interviews, no suggestive social media posts.

Real Madrid and - most importantly - new manager Jose Mourinho want him to stay and agree new terms. Sky Sports News reported on Monday morning that there will be further talks this week between Real and Vinicius' representatives, with Arsenal monitoring things closely.

Image: Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr is one of the most sought-after players in world football

Club president Florentino Perez is personally involved and has publicly expressed a desire for Vinicius to stay long term. Reports in Spain have long claimed that both parties have indicated a preference for him to remain at the club. Real Madrid do not want him to run down the deal into a free agent situation either.

Vinicius is more than just an outstanding left winger. He is a global superstar - and a Galactico in every sense. In that way he embodies everything about Real Madrid and fits right in.

Can the same be said about Arsenal? Signing such an icon has not been part of Mikel Arteta's Arsenal project so far, however exciting it might be to go in that direction.

What's the latest on Diomande?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande addressed speculation surrounding his future when he ws on World Cup duty - but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger

Real Madrid have upped their offer for winger Yan Diomande during talks with RB Leipzig, according to Sky in Germany.

They are reporting the offer, worth between £94m and £98m, has not been rejected yet, but further talks are required to satisfy Leipzig's demands.

According to Sky in Germany, around £102m is considered a realistic final price for Diomande, with Leipzig seeking a higher guaranteed fee from Real Madrid.

As things stand, there is no final agreement, but Leipzig are expecting the deal to be completed soon. Leganes have a sell-on clause for between five and eight per cent of the sale.

Diomande is at Leipzig and continues to train with the German club.

At the figures being discussed, Diomande looks set to become the most expensive African player ever, surpassing the £72m Arsenal paid for Nicolas Pepe in 2019.

Does Real Madrid's pursuit of Diomande impact Vinicius Jr?

Sky Sports News has been told Real's proposed deal for Diomande has no real bearing on the Vinicius situation. It says nothing about their desire to keep Vinicius, and only suggests they see a front three with both of these players in the team.

Diomande can play on the right wing as well, and he only strengthens the attacking options of the biggest club in the world.

According to Spanish newspaper AS, the players whose futures would be affected by Diomande's arrival are more likely to be striker Goncalo Garcia - who is wanted by Fulham - and winger Brahim Diaz. Rodrygo is still recovering from a long-term injury, so Diomande has space to come into the team quickly, even at only 19 years old.

What is the most likely outcome?

At this stage, all signs still point to Vinicius signing a new deal with Real Madrid. The fact that they will all meet again this week to discuss this suggests this is the direction of travel.

It will most likely come down to how closely Vinicius' earnings can approach those of Mbappe and satisfy his Galactico status in the squad. Normally, you do not say no to Real Madrid.

Real would not want to go into the new season with his contract running down and the resulting intensification of media speculation.

Arsenal's interest is likely to become more concrete only if the renewal fully fails, so this week is a crucial one.

Sports.title: Chelsea interested in Henderson after holding positive talks with Welbeck
Sports.content:
Chelsea are interested in signing Jordan Henderson from Brentford.

They are one of several big Premier League clubs looking to add his experience and quality to their ranks.

There is a realisation among those clubs that the 36-year-old has impressed at Brentford and with England since returning to the country from Ajax in 2025.

Brentford have been clear with Henderson since they signed him that they would not stand in his way if big clubs came in.

In that spirit, he could be allowed to leave on a free transfer, however that is not certain to be the case if multiple clubs come in. He has a year left on his Brentford deal.

Henderson has the character, leadership qualities and experience Chelsea are adding to their squad this summer.

Chelsea were keen on Granit Xhaka at Sunderland earlier this summer but a deal did not materialise.

Positive talks held for Welbeck

Image: Chelsea have held positive talks over the signing of Danny Welbeck

Chelsea have held positive initial talks with Brighton about a deal for Danny Welbeck.

With a year remaining on his contract, Brighton do not want to stand in the striker's way as long as they get a fair price for his sale.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Check out all 13 of Danny Welbeck's goals for Brighton in the 2025/26 Premier League season!

Welbeck has continued to be a reliable goalscorer in the Premier League at 35 years old. Last season he scored 13 times, after scoring 10 in the previous campaign.

His potential arrival would be another example of Chelsea prioritising physically imposing players with Premier League experience this summer.

They have already signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m - a record fee for a British player - and are close to bringing in Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix.

It would also place further doubt on the futures of strikers Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu.

Chelsea have signed several players from Brighton in recent seasons including their main striker Joao Pedro, plus Moises Caicedo, Marc Cucurella and Robert Sanchez.

A number of Brighton staff members have also moved to Stamford Bridge over the past four years, including sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell.

BlueCo's drastic change in transfer policy

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

Chelsea moving for a Brighton player is not out of the ordinary. However, Chelsea moving for a Brighton player in their mid-30s is.

Following that up with another from that demographic, despite them being currently injured, is a very deliberate ploy.

The BlueCo era has been defined by hoarding some of the best young talent on the planet and developing them in-house. That method has had some successes, but overall, it hasn't panned out.

There is clearly some recognition and accountability from the top brass about that. In bringing in Xabi Alonso as manager, they know they have lucked out in getting one of the most highly sought-after tacticians in the game. The Spaniard has clearly identified the need for experience and the club are following his lead.

The interest in Xhaka earlier in the summer were among the first signs of the shift. Even making a move for Maxence Lacroix is evidence of a change in approach.

The Welbeck move is surprising, but there is some logic that can be applied to it. Is he going to start every week? No. However, Chelsea's four senior strikers have an average age of just 23. Combined, they have made 269 Premier League appearances and scored 74 goals.

The Brighton veteran has 400 appearances and 90 goals on his own. To have that as your back-up to the young guns you want to develop makes sense.

Henderson? That's a complete 180 degree turn. Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez are two of the more experienced players Alonso has. If you had to pick anywhere Chelsea needed a wise head, you wouldn't say midfield.

Yet, they wanted Xhaka. They now want Henderson. Alonso may have been the man to oversee the blossoming of players like Florian Wirtz at Bayer Leverkusen. However, he clearly sees the values of opposite characters and knows Chelsea, and perhaps more importantly, he needs people ready now.

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino called to appear before Congress over Trump ties
Sports.content:
Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House judiciary committee, has launched an investigation into Fifa president Gianni Infantino, seeking documents that would detail the ties between soccer’s governing body and Donald Trump and his administration.

In a Sunday letter, Raskin wrote to Infantino and called for Fifa to provide any documents and communications related to gifts, payments or benefits provided to Trump and his associates, as well as the visitor logs for Fifa’s office space in Trump Tower, which it acquired last year. The committee also requested that Infantino sit for a transcribed interview.

Infantino’s relationship with Trump came under scrutiny in the lead-up to this summer’s World Cup. In December, at the World Cup draw in Washington, Trump was awarded a newly created “Fifa peace prize” at the Kennedy Center, where renovations were allegedly “rushed” on the administration’s orders to prepare for the event. Fifa opened its office in Trump Tower in midtown Manhattan last July.

Such scrutiny intensified during the World Cup. Trump made several calls to Infantino to lobby for a review of US striker Folarin Balogun’s controversial red-card suspension before the Americans’ last-16 match against Belgium. Fifa did reverse Balogun’s ban, but the political circus cast a pall over the US team and drew the ire of other teams and associations from around the world.

Alongside the leaders of Canada and Mexico, Trump joined Infantino for the World Cup trophy presentation after Spain beat Argentina in the final. The pair, who watched the final together in a glassed-in section of luxury seats, were met with boos from the New York New Jersey Stadium crowd when they took the field.

Raskin’s letter references the Department of Justice’s decision to “dismiss the indictments” of defendants in US government investigations into corruption in global soccer, including the 2015 prosecution of more than 20 high-level Fifa officials and sports-marketing executives.

“[Y]our election as Fifa president was supposed to mark a red-card break from a decades-long culture of corruption and scandals that dressed down world soccer’s reputation,” Raskin wrote to Infantino in the letter. “Instead, at the start of your tenure, you dismantled Fifa’s ethical guardrails and disabled the organization’s ethics committee by pushing out most of its members. This lack of transparency and oversight has since paved the way for you to ingratiate yourself with the Trump administration via tactics that a New York University law professor and one of your former ethics committeemen described as ‘legal bribery’.”

The letter also addresses Fifa’s World Cup ticketing policy, which is already the subject of investigations by several attorneys general in the United States. The use of dynamic pricing drew much criticism during the tournament, leading to massive surges and pricing out many fans from attending games.

“The most recent quid pro quo that Fifa and President Trump orchestrated is not a victimless crime. It hurts Americans. Fifa has taken its newfound favored status in the Trump administration as a sign that it may rip off its consumers, most notably, by employing illegal price-gouging and fraudulent sales tactics for the World Cup,” Raskin said in the letter.

The letter gives a deadline of 9 August to provide the requested documents and schedule the interview. Raskin does not have the power to compel Infantino to appear, given that Democrats do not hold the majority in the House, unless he garners Republican support.

Fifa’s interactions with the US government did not end with this summer’s World Cup. The US is expected to be the primary host of the Women’s World Cup in 2031, and the success of this year’s tournament has led many to speculate that the 2038 men’s World Cup could be hosted by the US. Fifa has been approached for comment.

Earlier on Monday, Infantino used a 15-part message on Instagram to denounce his critics, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives. He touted the World Cup as a success.

More than 200 Fifa members have endorsed Infantino ahead of the presidential election in March, but some associations have stood in opposition. The Norwegian football federation is planning to submit a formal complaint to Fifa ethics investigations over Trump’s role in the reversal of Balogun’s ban.

Sports.title: Mind the ever-growing gap: the Premier League keeps spending big
Sports.content:
The financial power of the Premier League is unmatched. The teams in England’s top division have collectively invested more than £1.4bn in new players already this summer (through disclosed fees alone), around £303m more than the 76 clubs from the Bundesliga, La Liga, Ligue 1 and Serie A combined.

These figures are the gross spend, so take no account of players sold to help balance the books. Factoring this in only increases the divide. The clubs of Ligue 1 and the Bundesliga are £203.4m and £72.2m in credit from their transfer dealings respectively. While La Liga (£163.1m) and Serie A (£124.1m) have spent more than they have earned, they are an ocean adrift of the Premier League’s net spend of £523.6m.

None of this is new; it has been the trend for many years. The worrying aspect for teams across the continent is that the gap between the Premier League and the rest may grow wider before the summer is out.

Despite their enormous outlay, top-flight English teams have spent about £230m less than Premier League clubs of 2025-26 had at this point last year. But only 25 deals were completed by the end of 1 July (which is when new contracts usually start, explaining why pre-arranged moves are often finalised then). It’s roughly half as many as the 47 that occurred by that date last summer. The expanded World Cup will probably have delayed some deals, creating a potential backlog of transfer spending that will soon hit the books.

Assessing clubs individually highlights why most might continue spending. Aston Villa, Brighton and Tottenham have already spent more in gross terms than in the entirety of the summer 2025 transfer window. Unai Emery has a net £109.6m burning a hole in his pocket following business which includes the departures of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans. Brighton will need a larger squad as they have a Conference League campaign on the horizon while Tottenham are hoping to improve upon consecutive 17th-place finishes. Their trading may not be complete even though they’ve already outspent their efforts from last summer, with Spurs’ net spend of £149.7m the highest in Europe’s big five leagues.

Chelsea also have a higher net spend than last year, even before their reportedly agreed deal for Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix goes through. Even if that transfer is not completed, would you bet against BlueCo throwing more money around, especially with a new manager to back? Danny Welbeck is the latest to emerge on the Stamford Bridge radar. Either way, Chelsea have already invested more in new talent than they had on this day last year. The same is true for Everton, Fulham, Manchester City and Newcastle, all of whom may have further incomings in the pipeline, too.

There are other clubs with work to do. The three promoted teams have only spent £8m more between them than Sunderland alone had at this point in 2025. Régis Le Bris added a total of 18 new players to his squad last summer, with fellow promoted sides Burnley (15) and Leeds (11) also hitting double figures for incomings. By these standards, Ipswich (with seven new players), Hull (four) and Coventry (three) must recruit further.

At the opposite end of the Premier League scale, Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United have collectively spent two-thirds of a billion less on new talent than they did last summer. The latest rumour mill gossip says the champions may make a move for Vinícius Júnior. If not the Brazilian then perhaps Bradley Barcola, though Liverpool are also said to be pursuing the Paris Saint-Germain winger. Neither player will be remotely cheap. United are believed to be targeting Ollie Watkins – he wouldn’t cost Vinícius or Barcola money, but neither would Villa sell to a rival at a reduced fee.

The Premier League also has clubs who have yet to make an outlay. It is unlikely Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland end the summer without spending a transfer fee as is now the case. It would be remiss of Palace and Sunderland not to invest when they are in European competition this season. As for Forest, like Chelsea they have had an insatiable thirst for player turnover in recent times. With Elliot Anderson having left for an enormous fee, replacements will surely arrive soon.

It is remarkable to think the Premier League may not be halfway through its summer outlay when £1.4bn has already been used for recruitment. The top-flight English clubs collectively spent £3.1bn on players last summer, with over £600m in the final week of dealing alone. That figure may be blown away by the time the transfer window closes on 3 September.

Sports.title: John Stones set for Inter move after shining for England at World Cup
Sports.content:
Inter are closing in on signing John Stones as a free transfer after the 32-year-old defender left Manchester City in June.

Inter and their rival Italian club Juventus were interested in Stones before the World Cup and the Nerazzurri are now in pole position to recruit him following his impressive form in England’s run to the semi-finals.

Stones made 13 appearances for City last season before being injured in December. Yet after being out for two months and staying injury-free, he was selected only five more times by City’s then manager Pep Guardiola.

At the World Cup, Stones started the opening game for Thomas Tuchel’s team against Croatia, was an unused substitute against Ghana and Panama, made substitute appearances in the knockout wins against the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Mexico, before starting the quarter-final victory against Norway and the 2-1 semi-final defeat against Argentina.

Towards the end of last season Stones spoke of his continuing ambition to play at the top level. “I still feel I have so much to give a club and I feel in a good moment physically,” he said. “There is a lot for me still to fight for in my career and a new challenge will be exciting. I’m keeping an open mind. I can take what I have learned here and maybe pass it on.”

While Inter are confident of signing Stones, the deal could yet collapse should a requisite Premier League club express an interest.

Arsenal’s William Saliba is out for an extended period with a back injury, meaning a defender is needed for cover in Mikel Arteta’s squad. Chelsea under Xabi Alonso are expected to play with three centre-backs so are in the market to sign at least one. Neither Arsenal nor Chelsea, though, are yet to make a move for Stones.

Sports.title: Chelsea explore surprise moves for Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson
Sports.content:
Chelsea are understood to be in talks over a move to sign Danny Welbeck from Brighton. The 35-year-old is a surprise candidate to bolster Xabi Alonso’s forward line after scoring 13 goals in 37 Premier League matches last season.

In a further unexpected move, there are also reports the club are in negotiations to bring in England midfielder Jordan Henderson from Brentford. The 36-year-old has a year left on his contract, but it is claimed the Bees would be willing to let him leave on a free transfer.

The former Liverpool captain made 34 appearances for Brentford last season and was a member of England’s World Cup squad. He broke his arm when he fell over advertising hoardings celebrating their win over Mexico.

Welbeck also has a year remaining on his deal and there is optimism a deal can be concluded as Brighton are understood to be willing to let the striker move for the right price.

Should a deal be reached it would increase the likelihood of departures from Stamford Bridge, with uncertainty surrounding the futures of Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson. Delap is considered second-choice striker behind João Pedro, who impressed in his debut Chelsea campaign with 15 league goals, while Jackson spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich and has attracted interest from Aston Villa.

Delap had been expected to be given a second year to prove himself after an unsuccessful debut campaign following his £30m move from Ipswich a year ago, though this latest development would seem to cast doubt on his future.

Interest in Welbeck and Henderson reflects a revised Chelsea transfer policy as the club seek to recruit more established players under Alonso.

Welbeck, who scored twice when Brighton won 3-1 at Stamford Bridge last season, signed a 12-month deal in March which runs until the end of the 2026-27 season. If the move happens, Welbeck would join a long line of players and staff to make the switch from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years, including the goalkeeper Robert Sánchez, midfielder Moises Caicedo and striker João Pedro.

Sports.title: Trial to be introduced in bid to prevent goalkeeper tactical time-outs
Sports.content:
English football will introduce a trial this season in an effort to end the goalkeeper tactical time-out.

The trial – backed collectively by Pro Ref, the Football Association, Premier League, English Football League, Women’s Super League and the National League – aims to prevent goalkeeper injuries used to disrupt momentum and allow opportunities for tactical instruction.

The new measures are pending permission from the game’s law makers, the International Football Association Board, but are planned to run throughout the course of the 2026-27 domestic season.

“As part of the trial, if the game is stopped for a goalkeeper injury, the manager/head coach will be required to nominate an outfield player to leave the pitch immediately,” the governing bodies said in a joint statement. “The nominated player is required to remain off the field for a minimum of one minute after the restart of play.

“The aim is to ensure genuine injuries continue to receive appropriate medical attention, while removing any potential sporting advantage associated with stoppages.”

The trial will operate with several exceptions, including when a free-kick is awarded for a foul on the goalkeeper and they immediately require treatment – also, when the goalkeeper and an outfield player have collided and need attention, or the goalkeeper is bleeding.

Last season the goalkeeper eight-second rule was introduced, punishing a goalkeeper for holding the ball for that length of time with the award of a corner to the opposition. That rule change was deemed a success and, working alongside that this season, a five-second countdown will be used by match officials where players have delayed the taking of a throw-in or goal-kick.

Players will also be given 10 seconds to leave the pitch when substituted, and this will come into operation from the start of the Carabao Cup on 1 August.

Sports.title: ‘Born out of quality’: Webb vows to increase match officials from minority groups
Sports.content:
Howard Webb, England’s chief refereeing officer, has vowed to continue increasing the talent pool from under-represented communities in English football’s officiating pathway, rejecting the wider backlash against diversity initiatives.

Addressing that historic under-representation has prompted a new direction. In June, the newly named Professional Referees’ Body (Pro Ref), formerly called Professional Game Match Officials, announced that Select Group 1, 2 and its supplementary list had been merged into a new, single Professional Referee Group in the men’s professional game and will largely service the Premier League and the Championship from the start of the 2026-27 season. Pro Ref said it would create flexibility in appointments and help to recognise a wider variety of talented match officials as part of the organisation’s new direction.

At a conference held at the Emirates Stadium by Bamref – an advocacy group that helps to give voice to Black, Asian and mixed-heritage officials – Webb told the Guardian that Pro Ref’s diversity drive fosters healthy and important competition. “We’re doing it to increase the quality of the officials working at the higher end of the game,” he said, insisting the decisions behind it are “born out of quality, rather than any other aspect”.

View image in fullscreen Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref. Photograph: Fabio de Paola/The Guardian

In March, Reform UK’s Suella Braverman wrote to the Football Association demanding that it scrap its target for a quarter of England men’s coaching staff to come from minority ethnic backgrounds by 2028, calling the approach “utter woke nonsense”. The FA responded by defending the target as part of its wider commitment to reflecting the diversity of the game. Similar pressure has surfaced in US sport, where the NFL’s Rooney Rule is now facing a legal challenge from Florida’s attorney general. In the UK, employers can encourage applications and provide targeted training for under-represented groups.

Webb argued that the visibility of refereeing makes tokenism impossible. “If you are not good enough to officiate in the Premier League you will be found out really quickly. There’s no real hiding places,” he said. A more diverse talent pool, he said, is “much more likely to bring higher levels of quality, greater choice, greater competition, and ultimately raising standards for all”.

Farai Hallam is the latest example, following Uriah Rennie and Sam Allison as the third Black referee to officiate in the Premier League. In a defining moment, he waved away a penalty claim for Manchester City against Wolves in January, rejecting the video assistant referee’s advice.

Danielle Every, the Pro Ref chief operating officer, said the organisation has seen a shift in attitudes since it introduced structural changes. “I genuinely feel that there is more acceptance and understanding of why these interventions are important,” she said, pointing to data showing zero Black representation among Premier League officials in 2022.

View image in fullscreen Farai Hallam rejects Manchester City’s claims for a penalty despite a VAR review during January’s Premier League match at the Etihad Stadium. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

The stance comes as Pro Ref overhauls how it identifies talent. Webb described moving away from solely relying on the traditional observer system – in which officials were marked out of 10 after every match and ranked on a performance table – towards a coaching-led model built around a new “matchday performance developer” role. That model will be rolled out in League One and League Two as well as the women’s professional game. In the Premier League and Championship, the key match incidents panel, a primary layer of accountability, will remain. Referees at all levels expect their matches and performances to be subject to review by individual coaches.

The old system, Webb said, was “very rigid and restrictive”, and led to “some really good officials being left behind”. The change, he insisted, will help to surface talent from under-represented groups earlier than before.

Aji Ajibola, who co-founded Bamref in 2019, welcomed the progress on numbers but warned it counts for little without sustained backing once officials are inside the system. “We now have a duty of care to those that we’re bringing into officiating, to make them feel safe,” he said, describing plans for wraparound support covering mental health and wellbeing alongside coaching and mentoring.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We’ve got expertise in our community, which then creates opportunities for us to get into other areas of the game,” he said, framing retention, not recruitment, as the next front in the campaign.

Tension between visible progress and lived experience was echoed by Akil Howson, inducted into the Bamref Hall of Fame at this year’s conference after becoming the first Black official in an FA Cup final. “Broken down the barrier finally after 158 years and now hopefully that door will never be shut again,” he said of the milestone.

Howson, who is entering his fourth season as a Premier League official, was blunt about how far the game still has to go. “I still go to some of my meetings and I’m the only Black person,” he said. “It’s getting better, but it’s frustrating because it’s not where it could really be.”

On his induction into the hall of fame, Howson pointed to what it signals for those coming through behind him. “It just goes to show how important visibility and representation is.”

Sports.title: Maldini and Leonardo resign from Italian FA after Pirlo appointment falls through
Sports.content:
Paolo Maldini and Leonardo have reportedly resigned from their roles with the Italian football federation in the wake of Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as Italy head coach falling through.

Both figures had recently taken on roles as part of an overhaul of the national team management. Maldini ‌was appointed ‌on 11 ‌July as technical director of the Italian federation, to help to rebuild the national side after they failed to qualify for a third successive World Cup finals. But he has stepped down just 16 ‌days later alongside Leonardo, the former Brazil international who had been brought in as his adviser.

Their exits come shortly after Pirlo said he was no longer in the running to coach the Italy side. His prospective appointment was the subject of fierce opposition over his commercial ties to a Russian betting company, Fonbet. The former Italy midfielder wrote on Instagram on Monday that he had “heard last night that I’m no longer the candidate for the Italy national team job”.

The double departure creates ​an immediate crisis for the newly appointed federation president, Giovanni Malagò. It leaves the federation without a clear national team strategy at its lowest ebb in nearly 40 years, following early ⁠European exits for Italian clubs last season and another failure ​to qualify for ​the World Cup.

Pirlo had ​been Maldini’s primary choice for the job after Pep ​Guardiola rejected the ‌federation’s initial ​approach. Several other ​high-profile managers are now being linked with the vacancy, including Roberto Mancini, Thiago Motta and Antonio Conte.

Sports.title: Spurs’ plans for new training facility in London park blocked by high court
Sports.content:
A council’s decision to allow Tottenham Hotspur Football Club to build a new training facility in a park in north London has been quashed by a judge at the high court.

The campaign group Guardians of Whitewebbs told a hearing in June that Enfield council’s decision to grant planning permission for a new women’s and girls’ football academy on 6.5 hectares (16 acres) of land in Whitewebbs Park was unlawful.

The group’s lawyers told the hearing in London that the council breached the rules when making its decision, as councillors were not provided with all relevant information regarding the development’s environmental impact, meaning they were “materially misled”.

Campaigners also claimed there was a “real possibility of bias” in the decision as Spurs had “unparalleled access” to senior council figures at the time of the application.

Enfield council, which was Labour-controlled at the time but is now run by a Conservative minority administration, withdrew its defence to the claim last month.

But Spurs continued to oppose the challenge, claiming it should be dismissed as the result “would inevitably have been the same” had the information been provided.

The club also said the allegations of bias were “completely overblown”.

In a ruling on Monday, Sir Tim Kerr, sitting as a high court judge, quashed the decision to approve the plans, finding the result “could well have been different” had all the relevant information about the scheme been available.

He dismissed claims concerning potential bias, describing the group’s arguments as “weak” and stating that “cordial relations” between the council and the club were “normal given the overlapping functions and interests”.

Spurs agreed a 25-year lease for the site in 2023 – a decision that was unsuccessfully challenged at the high court in 2024 – and the council resolved to approve the planning application in February last year.

The plans would have seen the construction of 10 football pitches and other work on the park, which is near the club’s men’s training facilities.

Jenny Wigley KC, representing Guardians of Whitewebbs, said in written submissions that the ecologist Giles Sutton had carried out a report into the environmental benefits of the plans in November 2024.

Sutton told the council that while he did not oppose the scheme “as such”, it was “counterintuitive” to accept the club’s claims that the site would benefit the local environment as about 40% of the park would be lost.

“In my opinion, if the council were to accept this, their decision could be easily challenged,” he added.

But Wigley said council officers had said in a planning report for councillors that there was “no objection to the proposed development”, despite Sutton telling the authority that this did not reflect his advice.

She continued that Sutton’s report “clearly informed the planning officers’ views” on the environmental impact of the scheme and should have been presented as a “background document”, meaning members of the public could have inspected it.

Wigley said: “[The law] does not permit this kind of salami slicing, where a planning officer can disclose parts of a report they agree with but can avoid public scrutiny of the parts of the report they do not agree with.”

James Maurici KC, representing Spurs, said Sutton’s views were “no more than an assertion” and that Guardians of Whitewebbs had “failed to provide any evidence” that it had been prejudiced by the council’s failure to provide the document.

He continued: “It is highly likely, indeed inevitable, given the absence of any evidence of prejudice, that the outcome for the claimant would not have been substantially different if the conduct complained of had not occurred.”

But Kerr said the council’s noncompliance with rules was “serious” and that councillors were “materially misled” by the exclusion of Sutton’s report.

Alessandro Georgiou, the Conservative leader of Enfield council since May 2026, said the authority was delighted with the decision and that it withdrew its defence as it would “not have been in the best interests of residents across the borough”.

He added: “We said we would protect Whitewebbs Park from this unacceptable proposal and we will now move forward with plans that reflect the needs of the local community and also preserve and protect this important area of Enfield.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino requested to appear before House Committee over Donald Trump relationship after World Cup chaos
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino requested to appear before House Committee over Donald Trump relationship after World Cup chaos

A leading Democratic US lawmaker has written to Gianni Infantino to ask him to appear before the House Judiciary Committee.

Rep. Jamie Raskin, the ranking member on the House Committee, has requested that the FIFA chief be scrutinised over his relationship with president Donald Trump.

4 Infantino has been requested to appear in front of the committee as his relationship with Trump is called into question Credit: Getty

During the 2026 World Cup this summer, questions were raised around Infantino and Trump amid multiple controversies.

The US president admitted that he had called the FIFA boss to overturn Folarin Balogun's suspension for their last-16 game.

FIFA then went on to announce Balogun was free to play against Belgium for the USA, with his ban suspended following an shock change of protocol.

That decision caused major backlash, and Infantino and FIFA were slammed, being accused of bending to Trump's wishes.

On top of that, even before the World Cup, Infantino handed Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize, while FIFA have used office space in Trump Tower in New York City.

Infantino and Trump relationship questioned

Now, due to those actions, Rep. Raskin is pushing FIFA to provide all records on its contact with President Trump by August 9.

A letter was sent on Sunday night and seen by The Athletic, who report that Raskin has requested Infantino to provide 'a list of anything of value (including transfer of money, gifts, prizes, awards, or public appearances) given to President Trump, members of his Administration, or their family members, or any entity associated with them, such as The Trump Organization.'

It has also been requested that Infantino and FIFA provide visitor logs for FIFA’s Miami and New York City offices.

Raskin wrote that his letter 'serves as notice' for all communications to be preserved 'between FIFA personnel and individuals affiliated with the Trump Administration or its inaugural committee — including disappearing messages exchanged on ephemeral communication platforms, such as Signal, Telegram, WhatsApp, X, and Truth Social.'

And at the end of the letter, Raskin asks that Infantino appears for an interview with the House Judiciary Committee, questioning whether the relationship between FIFA and Trump has gone too far.

4 Rep. Raskin has asked for records of communications between FIFA and the Trump Administration Credit: Getty

Raskin also requests all FIFA documents and communications since 2024 with any US official, or anyone associated with the presidential transition before Trump returned to power.

He also claims that FIFA's office space on the 17th floor of Trump Tower in Manhattan might ordinarily retail for $600,000 per year.

And the letter reportedly reads: “These actions appear designed to induce President Trump and his Administration to make decisions in FIFA’s favour."

As well as that, Raskin calls FIFA's controversial ticketing policy into question, with fans complaining over misleading ticket locations, variable pricing and 'higher-tiered' tickets.

“FIFA has taken its newfound favored status in the Trump Administration as a sign that it may rip off its consumers, most notably, by employing illegal price gouging and fraudulent sales tactics for the World Cup," the letter is said to have read.

“FIFA also introduced dynamic pricing, leading to sharply higher prices for many games. Even once a fan buys a ticket, FIFA may, at its own discretion, move them into a worse seat in a worse section. This is plainly unlawful, anti-consumer conduct … But President Trump’s DOJ and Federal Trade Commission have sat idly by, doing nothing.”

4 A White House spokeman has responded to the request from Raskin Credit: AFP

Raskin is unlikely to have the power to force Infantino to appear in front of the House Judiciary Committee as Democrats have the house minority - but it they take it back in November, further scrutiny could be coming the way of the FIFA president.

White House spokesman responds

The Athletic have also revealed a response from White House spokesman Davis Ingle in their report.

“Lightweight Jamie Raskin (is) a stupid person’s idea of a smart person," Ingle said. “No other president in history could have pulled off the historic feat that President Trump delivered for the American people and the world.

“Thanks to his bold vision and decisive leadership, the 2026 FIFA World Cup generated billions of dollars in revenue, created a massive economic boost across host cities, and delivered a safe, secure, and seamless experience for millions of fans and athletes from around the globe.

"It will undoubtedly go down as one of the greatest and most successful sporting events in history.”

Infantino statement

The call for Infantino to appear before the House Judiciary Committee comes after he hit back at FIFA's critics.

4 FIFA chief Infantino had already released a statement slamming his critics Credit: Getty

He launched a scathing attack on Instagram, writing: "To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness.

"Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.

"To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world.

"While you hide, we are exploring the streets of Canada, Mexico, and the United States, talking with fans, engaging with people and ensuring everyone's safety.

"While you divide, we unite."

Infantino suggested the World Cup experienced 'no violence, no incidents, 100 per cent safety and security, only joy and happiness'.

And he also claimed seven million people from more than 200 countries attended matches this summer.

Sports.title: Premier League and EFL begin immediate trial on rule change to combat dark arts
Sports.content:
Premier League and EFL begin immediate trial on rule change to combat dark arts

A new rule will be trialled in English football this season in a bid to clamp down on goalkeeper tactical timeouts.

The controversial issue drew criticism from managers, fans and pundits throughout the previous campaign.

2 A goalkeeper receiving treatment will affect his teammates who play outfield from August Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Goalkeepers will no longer be able to go down to receive treatment without a player leaving the field of play under the new rule.

It follows an agreement with the FA which will see the Premier League, Football League, National League and Women’s Super League trial the rule change this season.

The International Football Association Board (IFAB) have granted permission for the trial to take place.

Rule change trial

From the start of the season, teams must remove an outfield player when their goalkeeper receives on-field treatment.

Managers will have ten seconds to select a player to leave the pitch once the referee has signalled for the physio to come on.

If they do not nominate a player within ten seconds, the captain will automatically be chosen to leave the field.

The new rule will be trialled for the first time on Saturday during the Carabao Cup preliminary round tie involving Tranmere and Rochdale.

It is understood a variation of the rule will also be used in Australia's A-League this term.

However, their implementation of the rule will see the captain always having to leave the field.

FIFA also clamped down on the potential breaks in play during this summer's World Cup.

2 This trial should lead to fewer instances of goalkeepers receiving treatment from physios Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Players were not permitted to go to the touchline when goalkeepers were receiving treatment, instead gathering in the centre circle.

Controversial timeouts

This season's trial follows a rise in goalkeepers being perceived to fake injuries in order to force stoppages in play for unnecessary treatment last season.

Their teammates would then be able to receive instructions from the manager and coaching staff on the touchline.

Leeds United boss Daniel Farke publicly accused Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma of faking an injury in November.

His outburst followed City's 3-2 Premier League win over Leeds at the Etihad Stadium.

Speaking after the match, Farke exclaimed: "Everyone knows why he went down.

"It is not the elephant in the room. Why he went down it was obvious. It is within the rules. It is smart.

"If I like it? If it's within the sense of fair play? If it should be like this I will keep to myself. It is up to the authorities to find a solution.

"I ask the fourth official at this point if you want to do something. Our hands are tied.

"If we don't educate our players in football what to do in terms of fair play and sportsmanship and whatever and if we just try to bend the rules and even do a fake injury in order to do an additional team talk, it is not what I like personally. But if it is within the rules I can't complain."

Sports.title: James Trafford closes in on record transfer to new Premier League club after Newcastle interest
Sports.content:
James Trafford closes in on record transfer to new Premier League club after Newcastle interest

Leeds United are close to agreeing a deal to sign Manchester City goalkeeper James Trafford, talkSPORT understands.

Trafford has been keen to leave City this summer in search of a No.1 role at another Premier League club.

3 Trafford won two trophies in his first season with Man City Credit: Getty

The 23-year-old had indicated that he wants to join Leeds and he is set to become their highest-paid player.

Negotiations have been moving quickly and so much so that a deal for Trafford is now close to being agreed.

talkSPORT understands that Leeds will pay a club-record £40million plus bonuses for the wantaway England international.

Trafford joined the Etihad side last summer in a £27m deal from Burnley - just two years after City sold him for £14m.

He started in the opening three Premier League games of the season, before he was left blindsided by City's deadline-day swoop to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Trafford ended up playing just four times under Pep Guardiola in the league, but a further 13 games in cup competitions.

Man City won both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup last season.

Trafford heading for Leeds

Leeds have seen Illan Meslier and Karl Darlow depart this summer, to back-up roles at Arsenal and Man United respectively.

Lucas Perri joined the club last summer and made 15 Premier League appearances last season, but Daniel Farke will sign a new No.1.

And it seems Trafford is going to be his man, with the deal expected to be finalised this week between Leeds and Man City.

3 Trafford is set to be Farke's new No.1 at Elland Road Credit: Getty

Newcastle have held a long-term interest in the goalkeeper too, but have recently signed 20-year-old Ewen Jaouen.

Nick Pope remains on the books too, while Aaron Ramsdale returned to Southampton after his loan spell.

The Magpies have not held any recent talks or placed a bid.

The last conversations occurred when Trafford was discussed as an option when Man City explored signing Sandro Tonali.

Trafford blindsided

Leeds-bound Trafford initially joined City last summer with the full expectation of being their No.1 for the season.

But commenting on Donnarumma's transfer, he has revealed he wasn't told the club would be signing the Euro 2020 winner.

3 Donnarumma was signed by City on deadline day for £26m Credit: Getty

He said: "I didn't expect the situation to happen, but it happened, so just get on with it. It’s happened so I work very hard every day and see what happens, give it my best shot."

Trafford added: "No, it wasn't that, but it [the plan] wasn't what happened. It is what it is. It's football, it is what it is, you've got to keep grafting every day and the games that come, play as hard as you can.

"It's just another experience to add to my career and yeah, it has been good learning.

"Let’s take it a day at a time and try and work as hard as I can and whatever happens, happens.

"I’ve obviously got a contract, so don’t know what happens next season. I just know that I’ll just take it a day at a time and try and improve.”

Man City start their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth, while Leeds travel to Nottingham Forest on the opening day.

Sports.title: Ex-Manchester United striker Chicharito signs for club that has never played a game
Sports.content:
Ex-Manchester United striker Chicharito signs for club that has never played a game

Former Manchester United striker Javier Hernandez has signed for American club Atletico Dallas, who have never played a game.

Atletico Dallas were only founded in November 2024 and are a brand new expansion side set to join the USL Championship.



4 Ex-Man United star Hernandez has joined Atletico Dallas, who have never played a game Credit: Getty

Ahead of the 2027 season, the second tier of the United States football ladder is adding one extra club to its league.

There are also four new teams joining the USL (United Soccer League) League One at the start of the new campaign.

The Dallas outfit will be competing in the Championship and preparations are being ramped up for their maiden game.



Player and staff recruitment only started this year, with plans in place to hold trials to find people suitable to join the club.

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. MUTV is the home of all Manchester United pre-season fixtures. It’s the opportunity to watch new faces, young players, returning names, tactical clues and the first signs of what United might become over the next season. MUTV on Sky: £7 extra a month. Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

But they won't need a try-out for their first transfer in the club's history, as they're bringing in a name that is known worldwide.



Hernandez, also known as Chicharito, has signed for Atletico Dallas.

The 38-year-old has become their first and only player, starting his career at the club by helping contribute to their project.

He won't make his full debut in Texas until March 2027, when the USL Championship season starts, leaving him with eight months to watch the team get built around him.



4 Hernandez is a Mexico legend and will be playing in Texas, which has a strong connection to his home nation Credit: Getty

Chicharito has not played for a club since his contract with Mexican side Guadalajara expired in December last year.

But the ex-Man United and Real Madrid striker will now continue his career by taking a unique opportunity.

'I didn't come here to finish my career'

Speaking after his arrival at Atletico Dallas was confirmed, he said: “I've been fortunate to live the dreams that every young footballer hopes to experience. I've worn some of the biggest shirts in the world and played in incredible stadiums in front of passionate supporters.



"Opportunities like this, though, are different.”

Hernandez added: “I believe Dallas deserves a club that reflects its passion for football, its diversity, and its future. I want to help create a winning culture, inspire young players across North Texas, and give our supporters a team they can believe in from the very beginning.

"I didn't come here simply to finish my career. I came here to help build the future of football in Dallas.”

4 Chicharito scored 59 goals for Man United across his five-year-spell at the club Credit: Getty - Contributor

Chicharito's history-making move

As mentioned, Chicharito left Guadalajara at the end of 2025, after taking his club appearances to 121 following a second stint.



Before that, he played in the MLS with LA Galaxy, so he will have experience of the football pyramid in the USA.

Hernandez headed to LA in 2020 from Sevilla, whom he signed for when leaving West Ham and the Premier League.

He spent two years with the Hammers, scoring 17 goals in 63 games in all competitions, having joined from Bayer Leverkusen.

The forward played the most games in his career for Man United though, featuring 157 times and scoring 59 goals in five years.



On top of his club career, Chicharito also remains Mexico's all-time top goalscorer, seven years after international retirement.

4 Hernandez (middle) spent his summer working as a World Cup pundit in the States Credit: Getty

He netted 52 goals in 109 caps for his country from 2009 to 2019.

Now, Hernandez takes a unique step towards the end of his playing days, signing for Atletico Dallas in a historic transfer.

His latest move comes after he worked as a pundit during the 2026 World Cup in the United States this summer.

Sports.title: Tara Kirk leaves Peterborough United to join rival club in same division
Sports.content:
Tara Kirk has left Peterborough United Women to sign for rivals West Bromwich Albion Women.

Kirk, who has become a viral sensation on social media after some impressive form in 2023, spent four years with Posh.

2 Kirk (far left) has departed Peterborough after scoring 55 goals in 96 games Credit: Instagram @taramaekirk

The striker joined the Women's National League North side in 2021, but she has now departed to sign for West Brom.

The Baggies are in the same division as her now-former club, who were promoted to the third tier last season.

Kirk scored 55 goals in 96 games in all competitions for Peterborough, starring on the pitch and building a huge following online.

She has also made appearances for the Republic of Ireland's youth side, whilst starting her career with Leicester City.

Speaking following her move to West Brom, the 23-year-old forward said: "I’m so excited. It’s nice to get it over the line.

"I can’t wait to get started. Everyone has been so welcoming.

"I'm very fortunate with the way I’ve been accepted in the group, and I can't wait to do as well as I can for the club.

“I’m very impressed with the facilities. It’s really great that the women’s team get looked after so well here, and that was a big deal for me when joining.

“I’ve spoken with Siobhan Hodgetts-Still [head coach] and Martyn Irvine [interim head coach].

"They’ve both been super welcoming and it’s been great to meet them and train under them. They’re both very ambitious and that matches me perfectly.”

Saying goodbye

Kirk boasted an incredible record at Peterborough, and after achieving promotion last season, she's sad to depart.

The forward posted on social media after her exit was confirmed: "Posh, I wasn’t just at a football club, I was a part of a family for the past four years where I made many achievements as well as always wanting to get Peterborough United promoted.

"Football is all about new challenges, new experiences, new opportunities and so it’s time to move on.

"Posh fans, you have made me feel so so grateful and I thank you all for your incredible continued support throughout the years, I mean that with my whole heart. I am very lucky to have had you.

"My teammates, the staff and the club, I thank you for the best memories on and off the pitch, and will always carry them with me."

Peterborough Women's manager Jake Poole has also spoken about the departure of one of his stars in Kirk, saying: "Tara has played a massive part in the growth and success of Peterborough United Women.

2 Kirk played for Posh for four years, but she's now joined a rival in West Brom Credit: Getty

"We are grateful for her contribution, not just on the pitch, but as a terrific team-mate and person to have within the squad.

"We wish her all the best in her new challenge and I have no doubt she will add value to a squad wherever she goes in the future."

Sports.title: ‘Great bitterness’ – Andrea Pirlo being denied Italy job sparks shock double resignation
Sports.content:
Paolo Maldini has quit as technical director of the Italian Football Federation after Andrea Pirlo was not appointed head coach.

The federation's president, Giovanni Malago, opted not to appoint Pirlo due to his commercial ties to a Russian betting company.



5 Maldini and Leonardo have left their jobs just 16 days after being appointed due to the Pirlo drama Credit: Getty

5 Pirlo had been removed from the running for the Italy job due to commercial ties with Russia Credit: Fonbet

Pirlo had emerged as the leading candidate to succeed Gennaro Gattuso after former Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola turned down the post.

The AC Milan icon, who was part of the last Azzurri side to lift the World Cup as a player in 2006, had strong support from the newly-appointed Maldini and his adviser Leonardo.
