World.title: Inside the money trail: How SIU probe linked Lucky Montana to PRASA tender
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) says years' worth of tedious investigation allowed for the tracing of the flow of money from a multibillion-rand PRASA contract to luxury properties linked to former Group CEO Lucky Montana.

According to SIU spokesperson Selby Makgotho, the investigations, which focused on the controversial R5.6 billion Interpreted Security Access Management System contract, started around 2014.

This was when the SIU came in with a proclamation.

The contract in question was awarded to Siyangena Technologies.

The two properties linked to Montana are in Hurlingham, Johannesburg, and Waterkloof, Pretoria. Combined, they are worth nearly R16 million.

READ | Former PRASA CEO unlucky as SIU targets assets

Makgotho said investigators worked through years of money trails from PRASA around 2009 to 2015 while also analysing available evidence.

“We are confident that we have done this investigation, considered all the available evidence, subpoenaed all the required documentation, but also followed the money trail,” he said.

Part of the investigations also saw bank records being analysed with “due diligence”, as well as Montana’s income and spending patterns being analysed.

That was when they realised something was amiss.

“Those incomes do not tally,” he said

According to Makgotho, there was a property of R13.5 million that was purchased and immediately thereafter demolished.

“I think there were modifications that they needed to do, and again, the funds to subsidise all those things, in our view, do not tally. “They raised a very questionable relationship between the income that was received versus what was actually spent," Makgotho he said.

The SIU has secured a preservation order freezing two luxury properties linked to the former PRASA CEO.

In a lengthy statement on X, formerly known as Twitter, Montana responded to the SIU, saying they have “become desperate”.

He said the SIU did not obtain any order to freeze his assets.

READ | Discussion | Scopa grills Prasa over rands and cents

“The SIU approached the Tribunal which is equivalent to a court, not seek a provisional order, pending my filing of a notice to oppose, within 10 days. I was served with papers on or about 9 July 2026 and filed my notice to oppose last Thursday.

He damned the manner in which the matter transpired, even going to the extent of questioning the day on which the order was obtained.

“What surprises me is the SIU choosing Sunday, a holy day for many Christians in the land, to lie to citizens that it had obtained a preservation order against two of my properties. It is a blue lie. It obtained a provisional order to start the legal process. They chose Sunday to tell this lie, hoping this would have the biggest impact and present me as a criminal.”

He vowed that the SIU will not defeat him.

“The SIU and other Organs of State continue to dream of the day they will feed on the carcass of Lucky Montana. But this will not happen, not in this lifetime,” he said.

SIU confirmed that the preservation order is an interim order which seeks to invite Mondana on 11 August to show why this interim order should not be made final.

READ | PRASA Train Scandal | R7.5bn spent as trains remain unused

But he said their work does not end there.

“In a month, we are looking at instituting civil recovery proceedings so that we move with the speed that is required, but not only with the speed but also having gone through the witness statements and having done a thorough and meticulous investigation.

“We are convinced that we have a case that will be presented before the Special Tribunal in our favour," Makgotho said.

World.title: Code name 'wigs': Court hears Mapisa-Nqakula threated to clear tender funds
World.content:
PRETORIA - The High Court in Pretoria has heard that former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula allegedly threatened to clear funds from a defence tender account if her demands for money continued to be ignored.

State witness Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu detailed fresh allegations of bribery against her.

She accused the former Defence Minister of soliciting bribes worth R4.5-million from her between 2016 and 2019.

Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu said after repeatedly ignoring calls and messages from Mapisa-Nqakula, the request for 'wig' funds linked to a R104-million contract was cleared from the project's account as punishment.

READ | Witness alleges Mapisa-Nqakula demanded R2m bribe

Ntsondwa-Ndlovu says the word wig is code for money.

She claims the money had been transferred to an Air Force account on the instruction of a deputy chief financial officer, identified only as Nangamso, who she claims is the former minister's relative.

But the defence objected, arguing that the evidence is hearsay.

The court also heard Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu paid the former minister an additional R500 000 in two separate payments later that year.

The State has concluded its evidence-in-chief.

Cross-examination is set to begin on Tuesday.

World.title: Ramaphosa calls for African action on migration
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - President Cyril Ramaphosa called on Monday for African countries to work together to manage migration, as his government faces mounting pressure over attacks on foreign nationals.

Ramaphosa's appeal to the Pan-African Parliament follows weeks of protests against undocumented migrants in South Africa, where protestors have blamed undocumented migrants from elsewhere in Africa for crime, unemployment and strain on public services.

He warned that unmanaged cross-border movement could undermine security and social order, and said no country could address the challenge alone.

"As African countries, we have to acknowledge and address the conditions that drive migration in the first place," Ramaphosa told a session of the parliament, which is the legislative body of the African Union.

"We need to work together to address issues like conflict, instability, governance failures, poverty and social discord."

Demonstrations that began last year over undocumented migrants' access to public health facilities intensified this year as protestors demanded that they leave the country by June 30.

More than 160,000 foreign nationals have departed South Africa over the past two months, according to an AFP tally based on figures from repatriating governments, in one of the country's largest recent migrant exoduses.

At least four migrants have been killed in the violence.

'Sad and abhorrent '

The attacks were "sad and abhorrent", Ramaphosa said, adding that "we in South Africa deeply regret and mourn" the lives lost.

"We've taken a firm stand against hatred for people from other countries, xenophobia or Afrophobia," Ramaphosa said.

Ghana has called an African Union debate on the violence.

Two of its citizens have also petitioned the International Criminal Court to investigate "repeated xenophobic attacks", a move Pretoria has dismissed as "opportunistic".

South Africa, the continent's wealthiest nation, has long been a magnet for migrants from elsewhere on the continent.

World.title: 'Cat' Matlala Trial |Defence accuses security officer of tailoring evidence
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged hitman Musa Kekana claims he wasn't the driver of the Hyundai i20 police were looking for in connection with the murder of Vereeniging engineer Armand Swart.



The firearms found during his arrest in April 2024 link Kekana to the botched assassination attempts the state says alleged criminal kingpin Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala ordered.



A trial within a trial is now underway to determine the admissibility of evidence retrieved during Kekana's arrest.



Captain Phimi Sekgobela, who's the state's third witness, is now detailing how Kekana's subsequent arrest took place and what was retrieved.



The trial within a trial resumes on Tuesday with the state leading Sekgobela in his evidence in chief.



eNCA senior reporter Silindelo Sebata has the latest from the trial in the video above.

World.title: Overflowing bins: Pikitup promise falls flat as rubbish piles up
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Weeks after Pikitup promised to clear Johannesburg’s refuse collection backlog, many communities say little has changed.

Residents in parts of Sandton and Randburg are still living with overflowing bins, foul smells and growing health concerns.

They're questioning why they’re still paying for a service they say they are not receiving.

eNCA reached out to Pikitup for an update on the outstanding backlogs and when affected communities can expect normal refuse collection to resume.

The entity is yet to provide answers.

eNCA’s Nabeelah Shaikh reports in the video above.

World.title: Resignation won't erase accountability or prosecution - Expert on Andrea Johnson
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Independent Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) head Andrea Johnson's resignation does not shield her from accountability.

This is the view of legal expert Zola Majavu, who said that the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry can still make adverse findings against her.

Additionally, there could be considerations for possible criminal charges that she may be subjected to.

In a 17-point application to vacate office addressed to Ramaphosa and National Director of Public Prosecutions Andy Mothibi, Johnson wrote that “the recent five months or so have been challenging and the attacks on both my person and official capacity have been unprecedented.

READ | Resignation fails to shield Andrea Johnson from tough Madlanga questions

But despite this resignation, she still returned to the Madlanga Commission for the third day of her testimony

"Accountability does not stop on a mere resignation or the acceptance thereof. If that were the case, she would not have continued with her testimony. She remains in the hot seat until excused formally by the commission. "At the end of the day in the fullness of time the commission is not precluded from reaching and pronouncing whatever findings they may make or arrive at in relation to advocate Johnson regardless of whether or not at that particular point in time she would no longer be in the employ of the NPA or heading IDAC," Majavu said.

Majavu's comments also extended to questions about whether the resignation could be viewed as an attempt to protect the institution.

He, however, argued the other side, saying any reputational damage to IDAC had already been done and that concerns of such a nature are 'too late'.

READ | Ramaphosa accepts Andrea Johnson's resignation

Majavu said while he notes that the decision to resign could have very well been Johnson's personal decision, it does not shape or minimise accountability or the damage that IDAC has already suffered under her watch.

"If there were to be any reputational damage at the instance of the institution, that has already happened, and it's an ongoing thing. It may well be that the most sensible thing to do under these circumstances was to go the route that advocate Johnson elected," he said.

On the role of the NPA now has against Johnson, Majavu said her resignation ends the employer's ability to institute disciplinary proceedings against her.

World.title: Vodacom lifts targets after Safricom deal
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Vodacom is expecting to grow faster now that Safaricom is in its fold.

It now has a controlling stake in Safaricom, which leads the mobile market in Kenya and had more than 62 million customers in December.

Safaricom also owns the fintech M-Pesa which facilitates more than 100 million transactions every day.

READ | Vodacom boosts Safaricom stake to 55%

Vodacom raised its target as it reported a 6.3% rise in first quarter revenue driven by strong growth in Egypt and other parts of Africa.

The telecoms group has cut its dividend payout target to at least 65% of headline earnings.

Vodacom says retaining more capital will help fund expansion in fast-growing markets while continuing to support dividend growth.

The company has also raised its 2030 revenue target to R300 billion.

World.title: NDPP orders withdrawal of Dumisani Khumalo's charges
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - National Director of Public Prosecutions (NDPP) Andy Mothibi has ordered the withdrawal of charges against Crime Intelligence head, Lieutenant-General Dumisani Khumalo and six others.

The decision follows representations made by the group and an Investigating Directorate Against Corruption memorandum.

Mothibi says the investigation is yet to be finalised.

The matter may not be re-enrolled without his express written approval.

READ | Dumisani Khumalo arrest not politically motivated, says IDAC investigator

Khumalo and his co-accused faced fraud and corruption charges.

That's over the appointment of Brigadier Dineo Mokwele.

Last week, the now-former IDAC head Andrea Johnson conceded that Mokwele was, in fact, qualified for the role in question.

A previous witness also admitted that the industrial engineer was charged for a future crime.

World.title: Kindiki loses key intergovernmental role to Mudavadi in Ruto's shake-up
World.content:
Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has been stripped of the role of intergovernmental coordination. [File, Standard]

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki is under siege following a directive by President William Ruto through the Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service, Felix Koskei, that has stripped him of the role of intergovernmental coordination.

And through the stroke of a pen, Kindiki has lost the key devolution department that will now be handled by Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, who will be the link between devolved units and the national government.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Madrid wildfires advancing more slowly but remain “uncontrolled,” authorities say
World.content:
The wildfires tearing through the landscape just west of Madrid advanced more slowly overnight but remain “active and uncontrolled,” Spanish authorities said this morning.

The slower pace of advance allowed firefighting teams to battle the flames, and they identified three fronts, with the most active one located in the hills just north of the San Juan Reservoir, which contain several hiking trails and local beauty spots.

About 15 kilometers south of that hotspot, some elderly residents will be allowed to return to their care home in the town of San Martín de Valdeiglesias, said local official Francisco Martín Aguirre, the Spanish government’s delegate in Madrid.

World.title: AI devices that see, listen and record: Are we ready for the post-smartphone world?
World.content:
Picture this: On a normal workday, you and your coworkers walk around the office with tiny recorders clipped to your clothes. The glasses on your face nearly instantly identify what you see. Your bracelet records and analyzes all your conversations.

This is the future tech companies envision in the age of AI, whether consumers want it or not.

Major tech companies and startups are developing new types of wearable gadgets that can “see” or “hear.” Meta is selling millions of its EssilorLuxottica AI glasses with embedded cameras and microphones; Samsung will launch its own smart glasses later this year.

Wearing these items can give AI assistants instantaneous access to your life. Tech leaders hope that will help AI agents give advice tailored to users and, eventually, do things for you.

I personally tried to live in that future, integrating different wearables into my work and personal life. They were helpful in certain situations. But I often felt awkward asking friends and coworkers to record our interactions.

Devices that can watch you – and others – also put privacy at risk, experts say.

Unlike phones, they’re harder to spot, said Irina Raicu, director of the internet ethics program at Santa Clara University’s Marukkula Center for Applied Ethics.

“So the whole notion of consent is kind of disintegrating,” she said.

Trying them out

For years, tech companies tracked our lives via search trends, shopping habits, locations, and fitness routines online. Now, AI-enabled devices open up the possibility of using broader input from your real-world surroundings.

I wore three devices over the past several months – Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses, the Amazon Bee Pioneer wristband and Plaud’s Notepin S, a small recorder that you can clip onto your clothing. I took them to office, on work trips, even during vacation and at social gatherings. (The companies all provided them to CNN for testing.)

At times, I understood the appeal.

On a trip to Lisbon in April, I didn’t have to take out my phone to Google information about the Jerónimos Monastery, one of city’s most iconic landmarks. Meta’s smart glasses took a photo (with my consent), analyzed the image and came back with a response almost instantly.

I wore the Meta Ray-Ban glasses during my visit to Lisbon to learn about landmarks and take photos without reaching for my phone. CNN

The Amazon Bee Pioneer, a tiny recorder worn as a wristband that listens and offers advice, was helpful for networking events. It felt more natural to record conversations (with permission) without holding my phone, and the app suggested a contact for me to follow up with afterwards. The same goes for Plaud’s Notepin S, which I usually attached to the top of my shirt.

But often, these gadgets sat buried in my backpack or a desk drawer. That’s because using them socially felt strange.

As a journalist, I’m used to asking for permission to record an interview, but it felt odd during a game night with friends or even a one-on-one meeting with a coworker. Was the social unease worth taping these conversations?

A new wave of AI gadgets aims to listen to your conversations and provide advice or suggestions based on those chats. Ian Berry/CNN Photo Illustration

Things also took a weird turn at times. During that board game night, I mentioned moving to a new apartment in the fall. The next time I opened the Bee app, it reminded me to book movers for October, which was useful.

Then Bee said it thought my words indicated the move was triggering anxiety about “stability” and my “sense of home.” It suggested I photograph “one beloved corner” of my current space to take with me.

It was a glimpse into what could happen when AI assistants try to make conclusions by observing you instead of what you’ve specifically told them. I didn’t feel anxious about the move and certainly didn’t mean to convey that to anyone – not my friends, not my husband and certainly not my AI bracelet.

Amazon said Bee is designed to surface insights and recommendations based on what it learns about a user over time, and that insights can be less precise early on when drawing from limited context. Users can also mark certain Bee insights as inaccurate to help it surface more relevant advice moving forward.

“We’re constantly refining how Grow works, and the experience will continue to improve,” an Amazon spokesperson said in a statement to CNN.

The push for AI gadgets

My experiences are likely just a slice of where things are headed.

“Some of the largest companies in the world right now” are developing gadgets like AI pendants, pins and jewelry, Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon told CNN and a small group of journalists in June.

For Amazon, Bee is key to the future of its Alexa assistant. Most people would want a personal assistant that has context about their entire day, not just time spent in the house, Panos Panay, Amazon’s senior vice president of devices and Alexa, told CNN.

Plaud’s Notepin S can be clipped to your shirt to record conversations. CNN The Amazon Bee Pioneer bracelet can record conversations with the press of a button. CNN

“The more they know, the better off they can complete tasks for you, and help you do what’s next. That’s quite powerful,” he said. “So it kind of leads to this: What are the future devices that connect you to your assistant?”

Nathan Xu, the CEO of Plaud, thinks his company’s recording devices may one day create a shorter work week. He thinks what’s captured on devices could help AI models better understand our jobs with less prompting, potentially helping people get work done faster.

OpenAI is working on a family of hardware gadgets, President Greg Brockman told reporters on Thursday. As AI agents advance, Brockman said the days of keyboards and mice will soon be behind us.

“Clicking things and typing things, it was a phase,” he said. “It was never what we wanted to be.”

‘Misused in dangerous ways’

The tech industry’s rosy outlook is at odds with how many people feel about AI – especially AI gadgets that can record you.

None has gotten more pushback than Meta’s AI glasses. Women have reported that men have used the eyewear to film and post videos of them on social media without their consent.

That inspired harsh words from pop singer Lorde.

“Can I just say for the record: F**k the glasses,” she recently said on stage.

Meta is now taking down those videos from Instagram. And Meta’s glasses – as well as the Bee Pioneer bracelet and Plaud Notepin S – have lights to indicate recording. Meta said the glasses’ camera won’t work if it’s covered up.

“We’ve built privacy into the camera for the glasses from the ground up – a capture LED will blink bright white when you take a photo or video you can save or share,” Meta spokesperson Dina El-Kassaby said in a statement to CNN. “This light has no off switch so both people wearing the glasses and those around them feel comfortable.”

A picture taken on March 2, 2026 in Barcelona shows Ray Ban META AI glasses displayed at the Mobile World Congress (MWC), the world’s biggest mobile technology showcase and fair. Manaure Quintero/AFP/Getty Images

But lights on some devices can be difficult to see since most people aren’t looking at your wrist or shirt when talking to you.

Wearable gadgets with microphones and cameras are risky because they can be discretely worn in areas that are meant to be private like a dressing room, said Calli Schroeder, senior counsel and director of the AI & Human Rights program at the Electronic Privacy and Information Center.

“There are some real concerns with how this could be misused in dangerous ways,” said Schroeder.

But tech giants seem sold on the idea of computers that can observe our surroundings. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg suggested on an earnings call last year that AI glasses could give people a “cognitive” edge.

“If you don’t have glasses that have AI or some way to interact with AI, I think you’re … at a pretty significant cognitive disadvantage compared to other people who you’re working with, or competing against,” he said.

World.title: Iran “will never allow the United States to determine timing of war,” foreign ministry says
World.content:
Iran on Monday said it is not currently engaging in peace talks with the United States and will “defend ourselves for as long as our interests” require, after President Donald Trump paused the US’ bombing campaign following nearly two weeks of strikes.

Esmaeil Baghaei, the Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, said in a televised press conference that Tehran “will never allow the United States to determine the timing of war and peace.”

“We hold America responsible for the military aggression against Iran,” added Baghaei. “What exists at present cannot be called a ceasefire.”

Trump over the weekend halted lethal strikes, which had steadily intensified over the past 13 days. US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said Sunday the pause in strikes was to allow talks with Iran to develop.

The recent dip in attacks came as Iranian and Omani deputy foreign ministers have convened in Tehran to discuss shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Baghaei said those ongoing bilateral discussions, are “useful negotiations regarding the management of shipping traffic” in the crucial waterway and “are unrelated to the United States.”

“The goal is for Iran and Oman, as two coastal states, to establish mechanisms to ensure safe shipping in the Strait of Hormuz while respecting the sovereign rights and sovereignty of both coastal states and observing Iran’s security and national interests,” he said.

The foreign ministry spokesperson also condemned US-allied European countries, including France and the UK, for “complicity with the aggressor.”

“We expected the new British government to act more wisely than the previous government,” said Baghaei.

World.title: Iran war casualty count eclipses 600 as Pentagon quietly changes accounting
World.content:
The Pentagon updated its war casualty database Saturday, recording more than 140 additionally wounded and restoring the four soldiers killed due to Iranian strikes last week amid questions about a lack of transparency over the war’s toll.

The Defense Casualty Analysis System, or DCAS, also featured a new tracking category — “Overseas Operations” — for killed and wounded “starting July 7.”

When the new Pentagon data is combined with updated totals for Operation Epic Fury, 18 troops have died and another 624 have been wounded since the US launched its war against Iran on Feb. 28. The number of wounded is a significant increase from the previous peak of 482 observed by CNN last week.

The Pentagon drew scrutiny from media outlets and lawmakers last week when killed and wounded numbers decreased in the DCAS system as Iranian attacks continued. The 12 Democratic lawmakers on the Senate Armed Services Committee sent a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday requesting answers on what was causing the changes.

The Defense Department’s acting press secretary, Joel Valdez, insisted in a Thursday social media post that the decreases were due to “temporary data disruptions on the (DCAS) website.” CNN observed data glitches that led to fluctuating casualty totals when monitoring the DCAS site on a minute-by-minute basis last week.

On Friday, CNN asked the Pentagon for more details about the data interruption, but the department neither acknowledged nor responded to the inquiry as of Sunday afternoon.

Beyond the July 7 starting date, the new “overseas operation” category on the DCAS site does not include any distinguishing details or specify the conflict in which the casualties occur, and the Pentagon did not immediately respond to questions seeking clarification on what the category covers. The category features a by-name list of fallen troops, though, that includes the three Army soldiers killed in Jordan due to an Iranian strike and the soldier killed in northern Iraq last weekend during a controlled detonation of an Iranian drone.

The July 7 date coincides with when President Donald Trump claimed a new conflict with Iran began in a War Powers notification the administration sent to Congress earlier this month. (The War Powers Act of 1973 requires the president to end military operations within 60 days unless authorized by Congress to continue; the Trump administration argued that the April ceasefire with Iran stopped the clock on May 1 for the conflict’s initial period.)

Lawmakers of both parties have argued against the administration’s interpretation of the War Powers clock, though some analysts and officials contend that the act itself represents an unconstitutional limit on presidential war-making authority. Secretary of State Marco Rubio argued the law is “unconstitutional, 100 percent” during a May press briefing at the White House.

Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski of Alaska said to Hegseth during a July 21 hearing that she is “concerned” the administration is circumventing Congress through the ceasefire clock reset.

“The claim essentially allows the president to extinguish the War Powers clock just at the moment that it becomes legally inconvenient … avoiding the congressional authorization that the Constitution requires and the War Powers (Act) intends,” she said.

Davis Winkie’s work at CNN is supported by a partnership between Outrider Foundation and Journalism Funding Partners (JFP). CNN retains full editorial control of the reporting.

World.title: Egyptian, Tunisian FMs hail bilateral relations and regional coordination
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Emigration, and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty and Tunisian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Migration, Mohamed Ali Nafti affirmed on Sunday, July 26, 2026, during a phone call that the special nature of bilateral relations and historic bonds uniting both nations.

The two ministers praised the development of ties and hailed the outcomes of the 18th Egyptian-Tunisian Joint Higher Committee held in Cairo last September, emphasizing the importance of following up on agreements to boost economic, commercial, and investment cooperation.

Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations across various fields.

Regionally, Abdelatty briefed his Tunisian counterpart on Egypt’s efforts and contacts with regional and international parties regarding rapid regional developments to de-escalate tension and support stability.

He underscored Egypt’s stance calling for an immediate halt to all military actions, prioritizing political solutions, and intensifying Arab coordination to safeguard regional security.

Regarding Libya, Abdelatty praised the results of the Tripartite Neighboring Countries mechanism ministerial meeting hosted by Cairo on May 21, stressing the need to maintain its regular meetings to support Libyan unity, sovereignty, and national institutions.

World.title: Electricity Minister presents renewable energy plans to ambassadors
World.content:
Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Esmat met on Sunday, July 26, 2026, with Egyptian ambassadors and heads of diplomatic missions to present investment opportunities in the country’s renewable energy sector and discuss plans to expand international cooperation.

During the meeting at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the New Capital, Esmat reviewed Egypt’s strategy to increase investment in solar and wind energy, modernize the national power grid and accelerate the transition to smart grid technologies.

He said that Egypt offers many investment opportunities in renewable energy and electricity infrastructure, supported by an expanding network of international partnerships and government policies aimed at increasing private sector participation.

Esmat added that Egypt is working to strengthen its position as a regional energy hub through electricity interconnection projects with Sudan, Libya, Jordan and Saudi Arabia, as well as planned links with Greece and Italy, which will support cross-border trade in clean electricity.

He also noted that the updated national energy strategy targets increasing the share of renewable energy to 45% of total electricity generation by 2028, while continuing efforts to localize electrical equipment manufacturing and attract foreign investment.

Additionally, the minister reviewed the ongoing projects to improve grid efficiency, expand battery energy storage, upgrade electricity distribution networks and reduce reliance on conventional fuels.

World.title: Egypt, Bosnia discuss boosting tourism cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Sherif Fathy discussed with Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations Stasa Kosarac on Sunday, July 26, 2026, ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in tourism during a meeting at the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM).

Fathy highlighted the strong ties between the two countries and their shared commitment to expanding cooperation, particularly in the fields of tourism and antiquities.

He also reviewed the outcome of his recent visit to Bosnia and Herzegovina, including talks on advancing bilateral tourism cooperation.

The discussions focused on increasing tourist flows between the two countries, promoting their tourism products and expanding air connectivity to support travel and tourism.

The two ministers also explored cooperation in tourism training and capacity building, as well as mechanisms for activating a memorandum of understanding on tourism cooperation signed during Fathy’s recent visit to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

They further discussed participation in Expo 2027 in Belgrade, describing the event as an opportunity to promote the tourism destinations of both countries and organize business-to-business (B2B) meetings between tourism stakeholders to explore new avenues of cooperation.

Following the meeting, Kosarac and his delegation toured the Grand Egyptian Museum and the Giza Pyramids, accompanied by Fathy.

World.title: FM asserts Egypt’s full solidarity with Kuwait
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty asserted Egypt’s full solidarity with Kuwait, its leadership, government and people.

He also asserted Egypt’s condemnation of all unjustified attacks targeting the country’s security, stability and sovereignty.

The remarks came during a phone call between Abdelatty and Kuwaiti Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah as part of ongoing consultations and coordination between the two brotherly countries on regional developments and efforts to de-escalate tensions and restore security and stability across the region.

During the call, Abdelatty conveyed the greetings of President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to Kuwaiti Emir Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah and Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Khaled Al-Hamad Al-Sabah.

The two ministers also discussed regional and international efforts aimed at reducing tensions.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of an immediate halt to all military actions and escalation, a return to negotiations and prioritizing political and diplomatic solutions to contain growing tensions and preserve regional security and stability.

He emphasized that the security and stability of the Gulf are an integral part of Arab national security, underscoring the importance of adhering to the principles of good neighborliness, respecting state sovereignty and refraining from interference in the internal affairs of other countries.

Abdelatty also briefed his Kuwaiti counterpart on Egypt’s intensive consultations with a number of regional and international partners to advance de-escalation efforts.

He stressed the importance of maintaining close coordination and consultation between Egypt and Kuwait in the coming period and continuing joint efforts to support initiatives aimed at restoring security and stability in the region.

For his part, the Kuwaiti foreign minister praised Egypt’s commitment to continuous consultation with Kuwait and commended Cairo’s firm stance condemning the attacks directed against Kuwait.

World.title: Zambians Ponder Who to Believe as Hichilema and Mundubile Battle for the Presidency
World.content:
By Venus N Msyani

With the August 13 general elections approaching, Zambia’s political climate has reached a fever pitch. President Hakainde Hichilema and Brian Mundubile of the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) have emerged as the leading contenders, drawing large crowds and dominating national conversation.

Even campaign music has become part of the competition, with each camp trying to outdo the other.

Beyond the rallies and entertainment, voters face the task of assessing each candidate’s promises, priorities, and record.

President Hichilema is asking Zambians to grant him another five-year term, arguing that his administration has delivered on many of the commitments made in 2021. He acknowledges that challenges remain but says his government has laid a foundation for continued progress. According to him, a change in leadership would risk reversing gains made over the past five years.

Energy remains one of the most pressing issues. Hichilema says his government is investing in electricity generation, solar power, and other sources, promising that loadshedding will soon be eliminated.

On mining, he pledges to increase production, saying this will create jobs and business opportunities for contractors, suppliers, and communities near mining operations. He also emphasizes youth participation in the digital economy, arguing that technology and innovation can help young people create jobs and businesses.

Hichilema has made several region-specific commitments, including: A dual carriageway from Lusaka to Livingstone for Southern Province, an international airport for Western Province, upgrading Mansa Airport to international standards, and establishing a university in every province that currently lacks one.

He highlights achievements such as tripling the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), signing free education into law, restructuring national debt, and employing teachers, nurses, doctors, and police officers. He also cites the reintroduction of meal allowances and school feeding programs.

Hichilema warns that removing him from office could jeopardize gains such as free education and allowances. He frequently references cadreism and political violence before his administration, arguing that a change in leadership could return the country to those conditions.

Mundubile, meanwhile, argues that Zambia cannot afford another five years under Hichilema. Fluent in both Nyanja and Bemba, he appears to connect easily with crowds at his rallies.

He accuses Hichilema of refusing to reside in State House, saying it undermines transparency. Mundubile says that if elected, he will live there, adding that prayer would “drive demons out” if the residence is haunted.

He has pledged to declare his assets and liabilities, though he has not clarified whether this would be done publicly. Transparency has been a recurring criticism of Hichilema’s tenure, with opponents pointing to his refusal to publicly declare assets.

Mundubile also vows to eliminate cadreism and lists promises he says Hichilema has not fulfilled since 2021. He notes that Hichilema pledged to reduce mealie meal prices from around K120 per 25kg to K50, but prices have instead risen above K300.

He argues that fuel and fertilizer prices have not decreased and says farmers were promised 12 bags of fertilizer per season but have instead been sharing small buckets known as meda.

Mundubile points to the severe loadshedding experienced over the past four years despite Hichilema’s earlier promise that it would end. He says many businesses closed as a result, leaving families struggling. Loadshedding eased only months before the 2026 election, and he warns it may resume afterward.

He also criticizes Hichilema’s record on the rule of law, citing instances where individuals aligned with the ruling party were not charged for alleged offenses while others were. He argues that freedoms of expression, assembly, and movement are enjoyed primarily by UPND supporters.

Mundubile has promised to repeal cyber laws, saying Zambians should not live in fear. Quoting Hichilema’s own words, he says, “When the government fails to change the lives of the people, the people must change the government.”

He says he will maintain free education but improve its quality by reducing classroom overcrowding and providing free books, textbooks, and uniforms. Meal allowances and school feeding programs, he says, will continue.

Mundubile also promises to give mines back to the youth, equip them with tools, and introduce safe mining and environmental protection training. He says older women will be empowered through opportunities to sew and supply school uniforms. He pledges eight bags of fertilizer per farmer, declaring in Bemba, “ifi fyapwila apapene.” Meaning “this ends here.”

Promises continue to accumulate. At a rally on July 24, 2026, Hichilema announced plans for another international airport in Southern Province, to be located in Choma.

While listing every pledge is not the purpose of this article, the volume of promises underscores the importance of voters listening critically. Are the commitments realistic? Are they achievable? Why are they being made now?

Such questions may help citizens make informed decisions at the ballot box on August 13, supporting the democratic goal of free and fair choice. If objective listening is overshadowed by crowds, music, and appealing promises, voters risk making decisions based on excitement rather than ideas.

World.title: Clergy hail peaceful campaigns
World.content:
The clergy on the Copperbelt have commended the peaceful conduct of political campaigns, describing the prevailing calm as a sign of growing political tolerance among candidates and their supporters.

House of Clergy Zambia National Executive Director Jimmy Ng’ambi told the media in an interview that the peaceful campaigns demonstrate that political players now appreciate that elections are a democratic process in which differing views and ideas should be respected.

Mr. Ng’ambi said tolerance among political parties is essential to maintaining peace before, during and after the general elections.

He noted that people are now able to move about freely wearing the regalia of their preferred political parties without fear of intimidation or persecution.

Mr. Ng’ambi also commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) for introducing a campaign timetable, saying it has helped maintain law and order.

“The timetable clearly shows which political party is scheduled to campaign in a particular ward at a given time, and this has helped maintain peace and order during the campaign period,” he said.

Meanwhile, Kingdom Springs of Life Embassy Church Senior Pastor Reverend Trevor Muziya attributed the peaceful campaigns to responsible leadership and political maturity among contestants.

Rev Muziya said most political parties have respected the ECZ campaign guidelines by adhering to the designated campaign schedules, despite a few isolated incidents.

“From my observation, political parties have respected the ECZ guidelines on campaign schedules. Apart from the incident in Ndola’s Mapalo area, where two parties almost clashed, the situation was resolved peacefully,” he said.

Rev. Muziya has appealed to political parties and their supporters to continue upholding peace before, during and after the August general elections.

World.title: Investments worth US$19.07 billion actualised-ZDA
World.content:
The Zambia Development Agency (ZDA) has announced that investments worth US$19.07 billion have been actualised.

Addressing a media briefing in Lusaka today, ZDA Director General Albert Halwampa said the actualisation is for the period between 2021 and 2026, while 2,338 investment licences were issued valued at US$97 billion during the same period.

Mr Halwampa said the actualised investments were recorded from 838 licensed companies monitored by the agency, adding that the figure is expected to rise as more investors submit implementation reports.

“I would like to inform the nation that investor confidence has never been this high. It’s actually the highest ever in terms of investor confidence in the country,” Mr Halwampa Said.

He said the US$97 billion in investment licences issued over the past five years exceeds the US$70 billion worth of licences granted between 2007 and 2020, describing the achievement as evidence of Zambia’s growing attractiveness as an investment destination.

“The manufacturing sector accounted for the largest share of actualised investment at US$7.33 billion, followed by mining at US$6.62 billion, transport at US$1.60 billion, energy at US$1.43 billion, agriculture at US$669 million, construction at US$521 million, while other sectors accounted for US$901 million,” he stated.

He further explained that Lusaka Province attracted the highest actualised investment at US$9 billion, followed by Copperbelt Province with US$4.4 billion and North-Western Province with US$3.3 billion, while the remaining provinces accounted for a combined US$999 million.

Mr Halwampa said the monitored investments created 149,956 direct jobs, with mining accounting for 48,007 jobs, manufacturing 46,759, agriculture 18,627, transport 14,743, services 8,065, and other sectors 13,755.

He indicated that the government remains focused on increasing the conversion of pledged investments into operational projects through the Zambia Investment Deal Room, an online platform that links local and foreign investors with banks, institutional investors and international financiers.

Mr Halwampa has since encouraged both local and foreign investors to utilise the platform and take advantage of incentives offered by the ZDA, adding that the agency remains committed to supporting investment that drives sustainable economic growth and employment creation across the country.

World.title: Copper Queens open WAFCON campaign against Egypt
World.content:
The Copper Queens will kick off their 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) campaign on Tuesday with a Group C clash against Egypt at the Olympic Stadium in Rabat. Kick-off is 19h00.

The Nora Häuptle-tutored side has been in Morocco for three days following preparations in Algeria.

Speaking at a pre-match media conference, Coach Häuptle said the team is fit and ready.

“We can’t wait to start the tournament. Of course we had preparations in Algeria. Our players in camp are fit and ready,” she said.

The Swiss tactician said Zambia will be aggressive but will not underrate the Egyptians.

“We are wary of our opposition to Egypt. We are starting against Egypt, a footballing nation. We can’t underrate them, but we are focusing on ourselves,” Häuptle said.

Captain Barbra Banda said the mood in camp is high.

“The mood is very high in camp. The girls are excited to start tomorrow, and we can’t wait for the game. We take each game as it comes. Our focus is on the game against Egypt,” Banda said.

FAZ General Secretary Charles Chakatazya addressed the team ahead of the tournament.

“The coach picked 26 of you to represent over 22 million Zambian people. Most of you played at the World Cup and saw what happened. It changed the lives of a number of you. Those who have been there should encourage those who haven’t because another opportunity is before us,” Chakatazya said.

He urged the players to support the technical bench and play as a team.

“Let’s work hard, support the coach and the technical bench. We should support our friends; no pointing fingers. Once you are a team, when one makes a mistake, you cover up, correct the mistake and talk later,” he added.

Zambia will be aiming to better their 2022 WAFCON bronze medal achievement.

World.title: Hamukale seeks higher FRA maize target
World.content:
Agriculture Economist Edify Hamukale has called on the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) to increase its maize purchase target for the 2026 market season from five hundred thousand metric tonnes to one million metric tonnes.

In a statement made available to the media in Chilanga, Dr. Hamukale said the proposed increase is necessary given Zambia’s annual maize consumption and the looming climatic risks that could affect food security in the coming year.

Dr Hamukale, explained that Zambia’s annual maize consumption stands at about three million, five hundred thousand metric tonnes adding that with such high demand, a purchase target of only five hundred thousand metric tonnes leaves the country with a very narrow safety margin.

He observed that climatic risks such as the anticipated El Nino present a serious threat to production.

“Without maximum state storage, we are operating on a very thin risk margin looking at the year ahead, which does not look attractive or predictable,” stated Dr Hamukale.

He recommended that regardless of the current storage inadequacies, the presence of 2025 carry-over stock or budgetary considerations, it is prudent for FRA to aim higher this season.

Dr Hamukale further warned that El Nino is expected in the 2026/2027 rain season and is likely to bring drought and poor harvests in 2027.

He however, welcomed the government’s announcement of K347 per 50kg bag of maize noting that the increase of K7 from last year’s price was marginal and positive for both farmers and consumers.

Dr Hamukale added that maintaining a stable purchase price will help keep food prices stable and predictable over a long period.

World.title: Man commits suicide in Mambwe
World.content:
A 42-year-old man of Mambwe District in Eastern province has committed suicide by taking maize preservative tablets.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba has identified the deceased as David Phiri, who served as an internal auditor at Chadiza Town Council.

Mr Mweemba said that the matter was reported by the deceased’s cousin.

Mr Mweemba said that the motive for the suicide is not known.

However, unverified reports suggest that the deceased defiled a 15-year-old housemaid in Chadiza District.

“Brief facts of the matter are that the deceased was on Leave from work and had travelled to Mambwe from Chadiza to work on his plot in Jumbe Village while lodging at the Mambwe Town Council Guest House.

On July 25th, 2026, the deceased was seen drinking alcohol and playing pool with friends at a bar within the Central Business district, afterwards, he parted ways with his friends,” he explained.

“At around 02 hours, on the morning of 26th July 2026, nearby residents heard someone screaming from the direction of the deceased’s plot but did not go to check.

At 07:00hours, passers-by discovered the deceased lying motionless at his plot and immediately informed the police,” Mr Mweemba added.

Mr Mweemba said police officers visited the scene where the deceased was identified by relatives, adding that a physical inspection of the body showed no visible injuries.

“A strong chemical smell was emanating from the body and particles suspected to be from the maize preservative tablets were found near the body together with a bottle of whiskey,” he detailed.

He said that the body of the deceased was deposited into Mambwe District Hospital Mortuary awaiting burial as no foul play was suspected.

World.title: Voter education gains momentum in Chinsali
World.content:
Mafinga District Election Officer (DEO) Joseph Nonde says Voter Education has continued to gain momentum in all the wards of Mafinga South and North Constituencies as voting day draws closer.

Speaking in a telephone interview this morning with the media in Chinsali, Mr. Nonde described the voter education so far facilitation as a success.

He said the Voter Education Facilitators have performed extremely well, owing to the fact that the district has no community radio station and lacks a radio signal from the national broadcaster, ZNBC.

Mr Nonde pointed out that the VEFs are utilizing community engagements such as community gatherings, functions, and roadshows, coupled with door-to-door sensitizations to ensure that the right information reaches the general public.

“We are also taking advantage of church gatherings, public meetings, and open markets which are held in all the wards every week,” he said.

The DEO said the program is on course in terms of meeting targets to ensure that every electorate is sensitized on what is expected of them before, during, and after the election, despite communication challenges in some instances.

He added that the district has continued to maintain a peaceful atmosphere throughout the campaigns, stating that no violence has been recorded.

The DEO, however, said the district has witnessed clashes between political parties due to a failure to adhere to the campaign timetable, which was resolved amicably between the parties involved.

Mr Nonde attributes the peace prevailing in the district to the successful implementation of voter education by the VEFs.

The DEO has since commended the VEFs for the job they are doing in sensitizing electorates across communities.

He said the Commission’s activities, such as the liaison meetings for political parties where parameters, expectations, and zones were set, have helped in fostering peace and peaceful campaigns among political players.

“So far, this is what has helped us to maintain peace, and I wish to commend political parties for upholding peace since the campaigns started. As a district, we are happy that Mafinga is violence-free,” he said.

Mr Nonde further disclosed that the district is ready for the forthcoming polls next month, adding that currently, the Commission is sorting out applications for polling staff in readiness for the national exercise on August 13th, 2026.

He said by next week, the selection of ECZ polling staff will be underway, as human capital is a major milestone in the election process.

The DEO all activities leading to the successful implementation of the electoral process have been done in line with the Commission’s guidelines.

World.title: Mpulungu Clergy calls for compassionate campaigns
World.content:
A Catholic clergy in Mpulungu District has called on Catholic faithfuls to continue conducting their election campaigns with empathy and compassion.

Henry Chisoka has emphasised the importance of understanding and kindness in community outreach efforts, urging believers to prioritize empathy over mere rhetoric.

Speaking during his farewell message to the Christians at Stella Maris Parish during the Sunday service yesterday, Chisoka highlighted that genuine compassion can foster unity and positive change within society, which aligns with the core teachings of the Catholic Church.

He encouraged faithfuls to reflect on Christ’s love in their actions, especially during the election period.

“Social development, charity work, and politics should not be a battleground of hatred and division, but a platform for unity and understanding among all citizens,” he said.

“Political campaigns often become heated and divisive, which usually lead to unnecessary conflict and misunderstandings but as faithfuls we must strive to resist the temptation to engage in inflammatory rhetoric and instead focus on listening to different perspectives with an open heart,” he added.

Brother Chisoka further explained that prayer and reflection during this time is vital for the nation and fostering empathy can help reduce tension and promote constructive dialogue among candidates and voters alike.

He urged Catholics to pray for wisdom and patience as they navigate the political landscape noting that a prayerful approach can help voters discern their choices wisely and act with integrity.

He reminded the faithful that their conduct during campaigns reflects their faith and can influence others positively, adding that faith and politics can coexist harmoniously when guided by compassion and empathy.

Brother Chisoka has also called on political leaders to run their campaigns with honesty, humility, and respect for their opponents.

He said by setting an example, leaders can inspire their supporters to conduct themselves with similar compassion as true leadership is rooted in service and understanding rather than arrogance and divisiveness.

He expressed hope that the upcoming elections will be conducted in a spirit of unity and mutual respect as Christians must take political campaigns as an opportunity to demonstrate the core Christian values of love and empathy in the public sphere.

And Christians of Stella Maris Parish have praised Chisoka for his dedication to the church.

Center Executive Chairperson Carol Chomba who spoke on behalf of the congregation said the unwavering commitment of Chisoka to the church community is highlighted in his numerous contributions to spiritual growth and outreach programs over his 14 months pastoral stay.

“As a community we will continue to pray for you and we hope our collective prayers and well-wishes will serve as a source of strength for you as you move forward, carrying with you our love and blessings of Stella Maris Parish,” she said.

Ms Chomba said Brother Chisoka’s leadership and compassion have left an indelible mark on both parishioners and staff, fostering a sense of unity and hope within the parish.

She revealed that Chisoka’s kindness and devotion had positively impacted people’s lives both old and young because of his willingness to lend a helping hand during times of need.
